# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

INHALT DES NUTZUNGSHINWEISES (nur, wo die Quellen etwas hergeben; sonst Aspekt weglassen):
1. Verwendung: Aufrufkontext, Parameter, Rückgabewerte, synchrone/asynchrone Semantik.
2. Fehlerbehandlung: spezifische Fehlercodes, DET-/DEM-Meldungen, Verhalten im Fehlerfall.
3. Nebenläufigkeit und Einschränkungen: Reentranz, Aufrufkontext, Reihenfolgebedingungen.
4. Zusammenspiel: Bezüge zu den verwandten Requirements aus dem Payload.

<div class="ai-lang-notice" style="background:#fef3c7; border:1px solid #fde68a; color:#92400e; padding:8px 12px; border-radius:6px; margin:8px 0 12px 0; font-size:0.85rem;">ℹ️ <strong>Editorial notice:</strong> This technical guide is currently undergoing translation. The original reference version is shown below.</div>
  <p>Der Aufzählungstyp <code>Can_ControllerStateType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>) definiert die grundlegenden Betriebszustände eines CAN-Controllers. Er steht über die Header-Datei <code>Can_GeneralTypes.h</code> zur Verfügung und umfasst folgende Zustände:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>CAN_CS_UNINIT</code> (0x00): Der CAN-Controller ist nicht initialisiert.</li>
    <li><code>CAN_CS_STARTED</code> (0x01): Der CAN-Controller befindet sich im aktiven Betrieb (gestartet).</li>
    <li><code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code> (0x02): Der CAN-Controller ist gestoppt.</li>
    <li><code>CAN_CS_SLEEP</code> (0x03): Der CAN-Controller befindet sich im Schlafmodus.</li>
  </ul>
  <p><strong>Verwendung und Schnittstellen:</strong> Der Typ fungiert als zentraler Parameter für Modussteuerungs- und Abfragefunktionen im CAN-Interface (CanIf):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><em>Modusanforderung:</em> Über <code>CanIf_SetControllerMode(ControllerId, ControllerMode)</code> wird der Zielzustand an den Controller übergeben (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=76">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 76</a>).</li>
    <li><em>Zustandsabfrage:</em> Die Funktion <code>CanIf_GetControllerMode(ControllerId, ControllerModePtr)</code> fragt den aktuellen Zustand über einen Ausgabezeiger vom Typ <code>Can_ControllerStateType*</code> ab (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=77">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 77</a>).</li>
    <li><em>Zustandsindikation:</em> Vollzogene Zustandswechsel meldet der CAN-Treiber asynchron über <code>CanIf_ControllerModeIndication(ControllerId, ControllerMode)</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=108">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 108</a>), woraufhin das Interface die Benachrichtigung an obere Schichten via <code>&lt;User_ControllerModeIndication&gt;</code> weiterleitet (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=125">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 125</a>).</li>
  </ul>
  <p><strong>Zeitverhalten:</strong> Beim Aufruf von <code>Can_SetControllerMode</code> übergibt der Treiber die Modusanforderung direkt an die Hardware des CAN-Controllers (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=144">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 144</a>). Der Zustandsübergang erfolgt abhängig vom jeweiligen Hardware-Controller entweder sofort oder mit einer Latenz von einigen Millisekunden (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=144">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 144</a>).</p>
  <p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierter Nutzungshinweis auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikation R20-11.</p>
</div>

<li><em>Zustandsabfrage:</em> Die Funktion <code>CanIf_GetControllerMode(ControllerId, ControllerModePtr)</code> fragt den aktuellen Zustand über einen Ausgabezeiger vom Typ <code>Can_ControllerStateType*</code> ab (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=77">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 77</a>).</li> <li><em>Zustandsindikation:</em> Vollzogene Zustandswechsel meldet der CAN-Treiber asynchron über <code>CanIf_ControllerModeIndication(ControllerId, ControllerMode)</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=108">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 108</a>), woraufhin das Interface die Benachrichtigung an obere Schichten via <code>&lt;User_ControllerModeIndication&gt;</code> weiterleitet (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=125">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 125</a>).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Zeitverhalten:</strong> Beim Aufruf von <code>Can_SetControllerMode</code> übergibt der Treiber die Modusanforderung direkt an die Hardware des CAN-Controllers (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=144">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 144</a>). Der Zustandsübergang erfolgt abhängig vom jeweiligen Hardware-Controller entweder sofort oder mit einer Latenz von einigen Millisekunden (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=144">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 144</a>).</p> <p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierter Nutzungshinweis auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikation R20-11.</p> </div>

Du bist der KI-Kurations-Assistent des Dokumentationssystems autodocs (AUTOSAR).

RICHTLINIEN (bindend):
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

INHALT DES NUTZUNGSHINWEISES (nur, wo die Quellen etwas hergeben; sonst Aspekt weglassen):
1. Verwendung: Aufrufkontext, Parameter, Rückgabewerte, synchrone/asynchrone Semantik.
2. Fehlerbehandlung: spezifische Fehlercodes, DET-/DEM-Meldungen, Verhalten im Fehlerfall.
3. Nebenläufigkeit und Einschränkungen: Reentranz, Aufrufkontext, Reihenfolgebedingungen.
4. Zusammenspiel: Bezüge zu den verwandten Requirements aus dem Payload.
Umfang: 120–350 Wörter, gegliedert mit <p> bzw. <ul>; keine Diagramme.

The original reference version is shown below.</div>
  <p>Das Element <code>Can_ErrorType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>) ist eine Enumeration, die über den Header <code>Can_GeneralTypes.h</code> bereitgestellt wird. Der Typ definiert eine standardisierte Obermenge von CAN-Fehlertypen, welche typische CAN-Hardware erkennen und signalisieren kann. Verwendet wird der Typ unter anderem als Übergabeparameter in der Callback-Funktion <code>CanIf_ErrorNotification</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=110">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface S. 110</a>), um Fehlermeldungen eines Controllers (gekennzeichnet durch die <code>ControllerId</code>) an das CAN-Interface weiterzuleiten.</p>

  <p>Der Wertebereich umfasst gemäß <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a> die folgenden Fehlerzustände:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Bit-Fehler:</strong> <code>CAN_ERROR_BIT_MONITORING1</code> (0 gesendet, 1 gelesen), <code>CAN_ERROR_BIT_MONITORING0</code> (1 gesendet, 0 gelesen) sowie <code>CAN_ERROR_BIT</code> (generischer Bitfehler, falls die Hardware keine Unterscheidung zwischen Bit-Monitoring 0 und 1 unterstützt).</li>
    <li><strong>Bestätigungsfehler:</strong> <code>CAN_ERROR_CHECK_ACK_FAILED</code> (fehlgeschlagene Bestätigung) und <code>CAN_ERROR_ACK_DELIMITER</code> (Fehler am Acknowledgment-Delimiter).</li>
    <li><strong>Rahmen- und Prüffehler:</strong> <code>CAN_ERROR_CHECK_FORM_FAILED</code> (Formatfehler), <code>CAN_ERROR_CHECK_STUFFING_FAILED</code> (Stopfbitfehler) und <code>CAN_ERROR_CHECK_CRC_FAILED</code> (CRC-Prüffehler).</li>
    <li><strong>Arbitrierungs- und Buszustände:</strong> <code>CAN_ERROR_ARBITRATION_LOST</code> (Arbitrierungsverlust), <code>CAN_ERROR_OVERLOAD</code> (Überlastframe bei vollen Empfangspuffern) und <code>CAN_ERROR_BUS_LOCK</code> (Bus dauerhaft auf dominantem Pegel blockiert).</li>
  </ul>

  <p>Nicht jede CAN-Hardware unterstützt das vollständige Spektrum der spezifizierten Fehlertypen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>); der gemeldete Wert entspricht dem von der Hardware bereitgestellten Fehlercode (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANDriver&amp;page=52">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANDriver S. 52</a>). Als reiner Datentyp besitzt <code>Can_ErrorType</code> keine eigene Reentranz. Interpretation: Die Übergabe via <code>CanIf_ErrorNotification</code> dürfte typischerweise asynchron im Interrupt-Kontext des CAN-Controllers erfolgen. Allgemeine Änderungen und Historien des Treibers sind in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00441" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00441">[SWS_Can_00441]</a> dokumentiert.</p>

  <!-- annahmen: 1) Die Auslösung von CanIf_ErrorNotification mit Can_ErrorType erfolgt typischerweise asynchron im Interrupt-Kontext der CAN-Hardware – Begründung: Der Spezifikationsauszug definiert die Signatur der Benachrichtigungsfunktion, nennt jedoch keinen konkreten Ausführungskontext. -->
  <p class="ai-note">Dieser Text wurde von einer KI erstellt und basiert auf der Spezifikation AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>
</div>

=== SYSTEM PROMPT ===
Du bist der KI-Kurations-Assistent des Dokumentationssystems autodocs (AUTOSAR).
Verfasse den Modul-Leitfaden (<div class="ai module-guide">) für das classic-Modul 'can' im Release R20-11.

RICHTLINIEN (bindend):
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

LEITBILD (Umfang und Aufbau orientieren sich an den bewährten Adaptive-Modulleitfäden):
- 900–1600 Wörter in 5–8 thematischen Abschnitten mit <h4>-Überschriften, die das
  Modul erschließen (z. B. Rolle und Systemgrenze, zentrale Abläufe vom Start bis zur
  Nutzung, Daten- und Interaktionsformen, Betriebsregeln und Randbedingungen,
  Konfiguration/Instanzbezug, Verhalten im Fehlerfall). Die Überschriften sind
  modulspezifisch zu formulieren, nicht generisch.
- Ein Abschnitt „Verhalten im Fehlerfall“ und am Ende ein Abschnitt
  „Weiterführende Detailbelege“ (die wichtigsten Requirements/Dokumentstellen kurz
  eingeordnet).
- Jeder Absatz enthält mindestens einen Beleg (Requirement-ID oder Dokumentstelle).
- 4–10 Diagramme, wo sie Mehrwert bieten: Sequenzdiagramme für zentrale Abläufe,
  Zustandsdiagramme für Lebenszyklen, Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramme für die
  Einbettung, Aktivitätsdiagramme für Entscheidungen. Die Schaubilder der Spezifikation
  (Payload-Einträge mit "figure": true) sind Ausgangspunkt: übernimm ihre Aussage,
  wo sie den Text stützen, und verbessere ihre Lesbarkeit.
- Das Fragment beginnt mit <div class="ai module-guide"> und endet mit
  <p class="ai-note">…</p></div>.

AUSGABEFORMAT (verbindlich, nichts außerhalb dieser Blöcke):
<<<FRAGMENT
<div class="…"> … </div>
FRAGMENT>>>
Danach je Diagramm-Platzhalter genau ein Block:
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> seq
<JSON nach dem Sequenz-Schema>
DIAGRAM>>>
oder
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> dot
<Graphviz-digraph ohne Stilattribute (Farben/Schriften setzt der Generator)>
DIAGRAM>>>

Sequenz-Schema (JSON):
{"titel": str, "teilnehmer": [{"name": str}], "schritte": [
  {"art": "nachricht", "von": <idx>, "nach": <idx>, "text": [str], "pfeil": "voll"|"offen", "gestrichelt": bool},
  {"art": "selbst", "teilnehmer": <idx>, "text": [str]},
  {"art": "notiz", "ueber": [<idx>, <idx>], "text": [str]},
  {"art": "abschnitt", "text": str},
  {"art": "rahmen", "typ": "alt"|"opt"|"loop", "guard": str}, {"art": "trenner", "guard": str}, {"art": "rahmen-ende"}
]}
Antworten/Rückgaben: "pfeil": "offen", "gestrichelt": true. Zustands-, Kontext- und Aktivitätsdiagramme als dot.

   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00844]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall support dynamic\nL-PDUs\n, where the\nCanId\nor\nrelevant parts of the\nCanId\nare placed in the\nMetaData\nof a\nL-SDU\n.\n⌋\n()\n7.4.1 Dynamic Transmit L-PDUs\nDefinition of dynamic\nTransmit L-PDUs\n:\nL-PDUs\nwhich allow reconfiguration of the\nCanId\nduring runtime (\nCanIfTxPduType\n) or where the ID or parts thereof are pro-\nvided as\nMetaData\nof the\nL-SDU\n.\nThe usage of all other\nL-PDU\nelements are equal to normal static\nTransmit L-PDUs\n:\n•\nThe transmit confirmation notification\nCanIfTxPduUserTxConfirmationUL\ncannot be reconfigured as it belongs to the\nL-PDU\n.\n•\nThe Data Length and the pointer to the data buffer are both determined by the\nupper layer module at call of\nCanIf_Transmit()\n.\nThe function\nCanIf_SetDynamicTxId()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00189]) reconfigures\nthe\nCanId\nof a dynamic\nL-PDU\nwith\nCanIfTxPduType\n.\n[SWS_CANIF_00188]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall process the two most significant bits of the\nCanId\n(see [1, Specification of CAN Driver], definition of\nCan_IdType\n[\nSWS_Can_00416\n]) to\ndetermine which type of\nCanId\nis used and thus how the dynamic\nTransmit L-PDU\nshall be transmitted.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00673]\n⌈\nThe CanIf shall guarantee data consistency of the\nCanId\nin case of running function\nCanIf_SetDynamicTxId()\n. This service may be in-\nterrupted by a\npre-emptive\ncall of\nCanIf_Transmit()\naffecting the same L-PDU,\nsee [SWS_CANIF_00064].\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00855]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIfTx…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P34_360",
   "page": 34,
   "text": "7.4.2 Dynamic receive L-PDUs\nDefinition of dynamic\nReceive L-PDUs\n: L-PDUs that correspond to a set of\nCanIds\n,\nwhere the actually received\nCanId\nis provided to upper layers as part of the PDU data.\n[SWS_CANIF_00847]\n⌈\nConfiguration shall ensure that dynamic\nReceive L-PDUs\nuse an ID range or a mask and that the\nMetaDataItem CAN_ID_32\nis configured\nfor the\nL-SDU\n. Besides, the software filtering must be enabled for these\nL-SDUs\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00848]\n⌈\nUpon reception of a dynamic\nL-SDU\n,\nCanIf\nshall place the\nCanId\nin the\nMetaDataItem\nof type\nCAN_ID_32\n.\n⌋\n()\n7.5 Physical channel view\nA physical channel is linked with one CAN Controller and one CAN Transceiver,\nwhereas one or multiple physical channels may be connected to a single network.\nThe CanIf provides services to control all CAN devices like CAN Controllers and CAN\nTransceivers of all supported ECU's CAN channel. Those APIs are used by the CanSm\nto provide a network view to the\nComM\n(see [3]) used to perform\nwake up\nand\nsleep\nrequest for all physical channels connected to a single network.\nThe CanIf passes status information provided by the CanDrv and CanTrcv separately\nfor each physical channel as status information for the CanSm (\n<User_Controller-\nBusOff>()\n, refer to [SWS_CANIF_00014]).\n[SWS_CANIF_00653]\n⌈\nThe CanIf shall provide a\nControllerId\n, which abstracts\nfrom the different Controllers of the different CanDr…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P34_361",
   "page": 34,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00655]\n⌈\nThe CanIf shall provide a\nTransceiverId\n, which abstracts\nfrom the different Transceivers of the different CanTrcv instances. The range of the\nTransceiverId\ns within the CanIf shall start with '0'. It shall be configurable via\nCanIfTrcvId\n.\n⌋\n()\nExample:"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P35_363",
   "page": 35,
   "text": "Figure 7.2: Physical channel view definition example A\nThe CanIf supports multiple physical CAN channels. These have to be distinguished\nby the CanSm for network control. The CanIf API provides request and read control\nfor multiple underlying physical CAN channels.\nMoreover the CanIf does not distinguish between dedicated types of CAN physical\nlayers (i.e.\nLow-Speed CAN\nor\nHigh-Speed CAN\n), to which one or multiple CAN Con-\ntrollers are connected."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P36_364",
   "page": 36,
   "text": "Figure 7.3: Physical channel view definition example B\n7.6 CAN Hardware Unit\nThe CAN Hardware Unit combines one or multiple CAN Controller modules of the\nsame type, which may be located on-chip or as external standalone devices. Each\nCAN Hardware Unit is served by the corresponding\nCanDrv\n.\nIf different types of\nCAN Controllers\nare used, also different types of\nCanDrvs\nhave\nto be applied with a unified API to\nCanIf\n.\nCanIf\ncollects information about number\nand types of\nCAN Controllers\nand their\nHardware Objects\nat configuration time.\nThis allows transparent and hardware independent access to the\nCAN Controllers\nfrom upper layer modules using\nHOHs\n(refer to section 7.2 Hardware object handles\nand section 7.24 Multiple CAN Driver support).\nFigure 7.4 shows a CAN Hardware Unit consisting of two CAN Controllers of the same\ntype connected to two physical channels:"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P37_365",
   "page": 37,
   "text": "Figure 7.4: Typical CAN Hardware Unit\n7.7 BasicCAN and FullCAN reception\nCanIf\ndistinguishes between\nBasicCAN\nand\nFullCAN\nhandling for activation of soft-\nware acceptance filtering.\nA CAN mailbox (\nHardware Object\n) for\nFullCAN\noperation only enables transmission\nor reception of single\nCanIds\n. Accordingly,\nBasicCAN\noperation of one\nHardware\nObject\nenables to transmit or receive a range of\nCanIds\n.\nA\nHardware Receive Object\nfor configured\nBasicCAN\nreception is able to receive\na range of\nCanIds\n, which pass its hardware acceptance filter. This range may exceed\nthe list of predefined\nRx L-PDUs\nto be received by this\nHRH\n. Therefore,\nCanIf\nsubse-\nquently shall execute software filtering to pass only the predefined list of\nRx L-PDUs\nto the corresponding upper layer modules. For more details please refer to section\n7.20 Software receive filter."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P38_366",
   "page": 38,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00467]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall configure and store an order on\nHTHs\nand\nHRHs\nfor all\nHOHs\nderived from the configuration containers\nCanIfHthCfg\nand\nCan-\nIfHrhCfg\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00468]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall reference a hardware acceptance filter for each\nHOH\nderived from the configuration parameters\nCanIfHthIdSymRef\nand\nCan-\nIfHrhIdSymRef\n.\n⌋\n()\nThe main difference between\nBasicCAN\nand\nFullCAN\noperation is in the need of a\nsoftware acceptance filtering mechanism (see section 7.20 Software receive filter).\n[SWS_CANIF_00469]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall give the possibility to configure and store a soft-\nware acceptance filter for each\nHRH\nof type\nBasicCAN\nconfigured by parameter\nCan-\nIfHrhSoftwareFilter\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00211]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall execute the software acceptance filter from\n[SWS_CANIF_00469] for the\nHRH\npassed by callback function\nCanIf_RxIndica-\ntion()\n.\n⌋\n()\nBasicCAN\nand\nFullCAN\nobjects may coexist in a single configuration setup. Multiple\nBasicCAN\nand\nFullCAN\nreceive objects can be used, if provided by the underlying\nCAN\nControllers\n.\n[SWS_CANIF_00877]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf\nreceives a\nL-PDU\n(see\nCanIf_RxIndication()\n), it shall perform the following comparisons to select the correct reception\nL-SDU\nconfigured in\nCanIfRxPduCfg\n:\n•\ncompare\nCanIfRxPduCanId\nwith the passed\nMailbox->CanId\n(\nCan_Id-\nType\n) excluding the two most significant bits\n•\ncompare\nCanIfRxPduCanIdType\nwith the two most signi…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P39_367",
   "page": 39,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00281] is an optional feature. This feature can be realized by different\nvariants of implementations, no configuration options are available.\n7.8 Initialization\nThe\nEcuM\ncalls the CanIf's function\nCanIf_Init()\nfor initialization of the entire CanIf\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00001]). All global variables and data structures are initialized\nincluding flags and buffers during the initialization process. The EcuM executes initial-\nization of\nCanDrvs\nand CanTrcvs separately by call of their corresponding initialization\nservices (refer to [1] and [2, Specification of CAN Transceiver Driver]).\nThe CanIf expects that the CAN Controller remains in\nSTOPPED\nmode like af-\nter power-on reset after the initialization process has been completed. In this\nmode the CanIf and CanDrv are neither able to transmit nor receive\nCAN L-PDUs\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00001]).\nIf re-initialization of the entire CAN modules during runtime is required, the\nEcuM\nshall\ninvoke the CanSm (see [3]) to initiate the required state transitions of the CAN Con-\ntroller by call of CAN Interface module's API service\nCanIf_SetControllerMode\n()\n. The CanIf maps the calls from CanSm to calls of the respective\nCanDrvs\n(see\nsubsection 8.6.3).\n7.9 Transmit request\nCanIf\n's transmit request function\nCanIf_Transmit()\n([SWS_CANIF_00005]) is a\ncommon interface for upper layers to transmit\nL-PDUs\non the CAN network. The up-\nper communica…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P40_368",
   "page": 40,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00382]\n⌈\nIf an L-PDU is requested to be transmitted via a PDU channel\nmode, which equals\nCANIF_OFFLINE\n, the CanIf shall report the runtime error code\nCANIF_E_STOPPED\nto the\nDet_ReportRuntimeError()\nservice of the\nDET\nand\nCanIf_Transmit()\nshall return\nE_NOT_OK\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01126)\nNote for [SWS_CANIF_00382]: See subsection 7.19.2 PDU channel modes.\nIf the call of\nCan_Write()\nreturns with\nCAN_BUSY\n, please refer to section 7.12 Trans-\nmit confirmation for further details.\n7.10 Transmit data flow\nThe\nTransmit Request\nservice\nCanIf_Transmit()\nis based on\nL-PDUs\n. The\naccess to the\nL-SDU\nspecific data is organized by the following parameters:\n•\nTransmit L-PDU\n=>\nL-SDU\nID\n•\nReference to a data structure, which contains\nL-SDU\nrelated data: Pointer to the\nL-SDU\n, pointer to the\nMetaData\nand\nL-SDU\nlength.\nThe reference to the\nL-SDU\ndata structure is used as a parameter in several\nCanIf\n's\nAPI services, e.g.\nCanIf_Transmit()\nor the callback service\n<User_RxIndica-\ntion>()\n. In case the\nL-PDU\nis configured for triggered transmission, the\nL-SDU\npointer is a null pointer."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P41_369",
   "page": 41,
   "text": "Figure 7.5: Transmit data flow\nCanIf\nstores information about the available hardware objects configured for trans-\nmission purposes. The function\nCanIf_Transmit()\nmaps the\nCanTxPduId\nto the\ncorresponding\nHTH\nand calls the function\nCan_Write()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00318]).\n[SWS_CANIF_00904]\n⌈\nIf Bus Mirroring is enabled globally (see\nCanIfBusMirror-\ningSupport\n) and has been activated with a call to\nCanIf_EnableBusMirroring\n()\nfor a\nCAN Controller\n, the\nCanIf\nshall store the content of each frame before it\nis transmitted on that controller with\nCan_Write()\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01172)\nNote: The frame content should only be provided to the Bus Mirroring module when it\nwas actually sent. Therefore, the content has to be stored so that it can be provided to\nthe Bus Mirroring module from within the\nCanIf_TxConfirmation()\n."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P42_370",
   "page": 42,
   "text": "7.11 Transmit buffering\n7.11.1 General behavior\nAt the scope of\nCanIf\nthe transmit process starts with the call of\nCanIf_Transmit()\nand it ends with invocation of upper layer module's callback service\n<User_TxCon-\nfirmation>()\n. During the transmit process\nCanIf\n,\nCanDrv\nand the CAN Mailbox\naltogether shall store the\nL-PDU\nto be transmitted only once at a single location. De-\npending on the transmit method, these are:\n•\nThe CAN hardware transmit object or\n•\nThe\nTransmit L-PDU Buffer\ninside\nCanIf\n, if transmit buffering is enabled.\nFor triggered transmission,\nCanIf\nonly has to store the transmit request for the given\nL-PDU\nbut not its data. The data is fetched just in time by means of the trigger transmit\nfunction when the\nHTH\nis free (again). A single\nTx L-PDU\n, requested for transmission,\nshall never be stored twice. This behavior corresponds to the usual way of periodic\ncommunication on the CAN network.\nIf transmit buffering is enabled,\nCanIf\nwill store a\nTx L-PDU\nin a\nCanIf Trans-\nmit L-PDU Buffer\n(\nCanIfBufferCfg\n), if it is rejected by\nCanDrv\nat\nTransmit\nRequest\n.\nBasically, the overall buffer in\nCanIf\nfor buffering\nTx L-PDUs\nconsits of one or multi-\nple\nCanIfBufferCfg\n(see\nCanIfBufferCfg\n). Whereas each\nCanIfBufferCfg\nis\nassigned to one or multiple dedicated\nCanIfBufferHthRef\n(see\nCanIfBuffer-\nHthRef\n) and can be configured to buffer one or multiple\nTx L-PDUs\n. But as al…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P43_371",
   "page": 43,
   "text": "needed as well. In this case, the buffer size (see\nCanIfBufferSize\n) of the\nCan-\nIfBufferCfg\nhas to be set to\n0\n. Then\nCanIfBufferCfg\nconfiguration container is\nonly used to refer a\nHTH\n.\n7.11.2 Buffer characteristics\nCanIfTxPduBufferRef\n,\nCanIfBufferCfg\n,\nCanIfBufferHthRef\nand\nCanIf-\nBufferSize\ndescribe the possible\nCanIfBufferCfg\nconfigurations.\n7.11.2.1 Storage of L-PDUs in the transmit L-PDU buffer\nCanIf\ntries to store a new\nTransmit L-PDU\nor its\nTransmit Request\nin the\nTransmit L-PDU Buffer\nonly, if\nCanDrv\nreturn\nCAN_BUSY\nduring a call of\nCan_-\nWrite()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00381]).\n[SWS_CANIF_00063]\n⌈\nThe\nCanIf\nshall support buffering of a CAN L-PDU for\nBa-\nsicCAN\ntransmission in the\nCanIf\n, if parameter\nCanIfPublicTxBuffering\n(see\nCanIfPublicTxBuffering\n) is enabled.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01020)\n[SWS_CANIF_00849]\n⌈\nFor dynamic\nTransmit L-PDUs\n, also the\nCanId\nhas to be\nstored in the\nCanIfTxBuffer\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00381]\n⌈\nIf transmit buffering is enabled (see [SWS_CANIF_00063])\nand if the call of\nCan_Write()\nfor a PDU configured for direct transmission returns\nwith\nCAN_BUSY\n,\nCanIf\nshall check if it is possible to buffer the\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\n,\nwhich was requested to be transmitted via\nCan_Write()\nin a\nCanIfTxBuffer\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01126)\nWhen the call of\nCan_Write()\nreturns with\nCAN_BUSY\n,\nCanDrv\nhas rejected the\nrequested transmission of the\nL-PDU\n(see [1]) because there is no free hardwar…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P44_372",
   "page": 44,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00835]\n⌈\nWhen\nCanIf\nchecks whether it is possible to buffer\na\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nor a\nTransmit Request\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00381],\n[SWS_CANIF_00881]), this shall only be possible, if the\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nis as-\nsigned (see\nCanIfTxPduBufferRef\n) to a\nCanIfBufferCfg\n(see\nCanIfBuffer-\nCfg\n), which is configured with a buffer size (see\nCanIfBufferSize\n) bigger than\nzero.\n⌋\n()\nThe buffer size of any\nCanIfTxBuffer\nis only configurable bigger than zero, if transmit\nbuffering is enabled. Additionally the buffer size of a single\nCanIfTxBuffer\nis only\nconfigurable bigger than zero if the\nCanIfTxBuffer\nis not assigned to a FullCAN\nHTH\n(see\nCanIfBufferSize\n).\n[SWS_CANIF_00836]\n⌈\nIf it is possible to buffer a\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nor a\nTransmit\nRequest\n, because the buffer size of the assigned\nCanIfTxBuffer\nis bigger than zero\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00835]),\nCanIf\nshall buffer a\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nor the\nTransmit\nRequest\nin a free buffer element of the assigned\nCanIfTxBuffer\n, if the\nCanIf Tx\nL-PDU\nor the\nTransmit Request\nis not already buffered in the\nCanIfTxBuffer\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00068]\n⌈\nIf it is possible to buffer a\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nor a\nTransmit\nRequest\n, because the buffer size of the assigned\nCanIfTxBuffer\nis bigger than\nzero (see [SWS_CANIF_00835]),\nCanIf\nshall overwrite direct transmitted\nCanIf Tx\nL-PDU\nin the assigned\nCanIfTxBuffer\n, if the\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nis already buffered\nin the\nCanIfTxBuffer…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P45_373",
   "page": 45,
   "text": "Requests\nare stored within the\nCanIfTxBuffers\n, which are assigned to the new\nfree\nHardware Transmit Object\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00466]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00668]\n⌈\nIf pending\nCanIf Tx L-PDUs\nor\nTransmit Requests\nare\navailable in the\nCanIfTxBuffers\nas per [SWS_CANIF_00386], then\nCanIf\nshall\ncall\nCan_Write()\nfor that pending\nCanIf Tx L-PDU\nor\nTransmit Requests\n(of\nthe one assigned to the new\nHardware Transmit Object\n) with the highest priority\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00070]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00070]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall transmit\nL-PDUs\nor\nTransmit Requests\nstored\nin the\nTransmit L-PDU Buffers\nin priority order (see [12, ISO 11898-1:2015]) per\neach\nHTH\n.\nCanIf\nshall not differentiate between\nL-PDUs\nand\nTransmit Requests\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00183]\n⌈\nWhen\nCanIf\ncalls the function\nCan_Write()\nfor prioritized\nL-PDUs\nand\nTransmit Requests\nstored in\nCanIfTxBuffer\nand the return value of\nCan_Write()\nis\nE_OK\n, then\nCanIf\nshall remove this\nL-PDU\nor\nTransmit Request\nfrom the\nTransmit L-PDU Buffer\nimmediately, before the transmit confirmation re-\nturns.\n⌋\n()\nThe behavior specified in [SWS_CANIF_00183] simplifies the choice of the new trans-\nmit\nL-PDU\nstored in the\nTransmit L-PDU Buffer\n.\n7.11.2.3 Initialization of transmit L-PDU buffers\n[SWS_CANIF_00387]\n⌈\nWhen function\nCanIf_Init()\nis called,\nCanIf\nshall initialize\nevery\nTransmit L-PDU Buffer\nassigned to\nCanIf\n.\n⌋\n()\nThe requirement [SWS_CANIF_00387] is necessary…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P46_374",
   "page": 46,
   "text": "7.12 Transmit confirmation\nIf a previous transmit request is completed successfully,\nCanDrv\nnotifies it to\nCanIf\nby the call of\nCanIf_TxConfirmation()\n([SWS_CANIF_00007]).\n[SWS_CANIF_00905]\n⌈\nIf Bus Mirroring is enabled globally (see\nCanIfBusMirror-\ningSupport\n) and has been activated with a call to\nCanIf_EnableBusMirroring\n()\nfor a\nCAN Controller\n, the\nCanIf\nshall call\nMirror_ReportCanFrame()\nfor\neach frame transmission on that controller that is confirmed with\nCanIf_TxConfir-\nmation()\n, providing the stored content and the actual\nCAN ID\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01172)\n[SWS_CANIF_00383]\n⌈\nWhen callback notification\nCanIf_TxConfirma-\ntion()\nis called,\nCanIf\nshall identify the upper layer communication layer\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00414]), which is linked to the successfully transmitted\nL-PDU\n,\nand shall notify it about the performed transmission by call of\nCanIf\n's transmit\nconfirmation service\n<User_TxConfirmation>(E_OK)\n.\n⌋\n()\nNote for [SWS_CANIF_00383]: See section 7.12 Transmit confirmation.\nThe callback service\n<User_TxConfirmation>()\nis implemented by the notified\nupper layer module.\nAn upper communication layer module can be designed or configured in a way, that\ntransmit confirmations can be processed with single or multiple callback services for\ndifferent\nL-PDUs\nor groups of\nL-PDUs\n. All that services are called by\nCanIf\nat transmit\nconfirmation of the corresponding L-PDU transmission…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P47_375",
   "page": 47,
   "text": "In case of a new reception of an\nL-PDU CanDrv\ncalls\nCanIf_RxIndication()\n(refer\nto [SWS_CANIF_00006]) of\nCanIf\n. The access to the\nL-PDU\nspecific data is orga-\nnized by these parameters:\n•\nHardware Receive Handle (\nHRH\n)\n•\nReceived CAN Identifier (CanId)\n•\nReceived Data Length\n•\nReference to\nReceived L-PDU\nThe\nReceived L-PDU\nis hardware dependent (nibble and byte ordering, access type)\nand allocated to the lowest layer in the communication system - to\nCanDrv\n.\nHRH\nserves\nas a link between\nCanDrv\nand the upper layer module using the\nL-PDU\n. The\nHRH\nidentifies one CAN hardware receive object, where a new\nCAN L-PDU\nwas received.\nAfter the indication of a received\nL-PDU\nby\nCanDrv\n(\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nis\ncalled) the\nCanIf\nshall proceed as described in 7.14 Receive indication.\nCanIf\nis\nnot able to recognize, whether\nCanDrv\nuses temporary buffering or a direct hardware\naccess. It expects normalized\nL-PDU\ndata in calls of the\nCanIf_RxIndication()\n.\nThe CAN hardware receive object is locked until the end of the copy process to the tem-\nporary or upper layer module buffer. The hardware object will be immediately released\nafter\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nof\nCanIf\nreturns to avoid loss of data.\nCanDrv\n,\nCanIf\nand the upper layer module, which belongs to the received\nL-PDU\n,\naccess the same temporary intermediate buffer, which can be located either in the CAN\nhardware receive object of the\nCAN…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P48_376",
   "page": 48,
   "text": "Figure 7.6: Receive data flow\n7.14 Receive indication\nA call of\nCanIf_RxIndication()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00006]) references in its pa-\nrameters a newly received CAN L-PDU. If the function\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nis"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,

   "text": "called, the CanIf evaluates the CAN L-PDU for acceptance and prepares the\nL-SDU\nfor later access by the upper communication layers. The CanIf notifies upper layer\nmodules about this asynchronous event using\n<User_RxIndication>()\n(see sub-\nsubsection 8.6.3.3 <User_RxIndication>, [SWS_CANIF_00012]), if configured and if\nthis CAN L-PDU is successfully detected and accepted for further processing. The\ndetailed requirements for this behavior follow here.\n[SWS_CANIF_00906]\n⌈\nIf Bus Mirroring is enabled globally (see\nCanIfBusMirror-\ningSupport\n) and has been activated with a call to\nCanIf_EnableBusMirroring\n()\nfor a\nCAN Controller\n, the\nCanIf\nshall call\nMirror_ReportCanFrame()\nfor\neach frame reception on that controller that is indicated with\nCanIf_RxIndication\n()\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01172)\n[SWS_CANIF_00389]\n⌈\nIf the function\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nis called, the\nCanIf\nshall process the Software Filtering on the received L-PDU, if configured (see multi-\nplicity of\nCanIfHrhRangeCfg\nequals\n0\n::\n\u0003\n). If Software Filtering rejects the received\nL-PDU, the CanIf shall end the receive indication for that call of\nCanIf_RxIndica-\ntion()\n.\n⌋\n()\nNote for [SWS_CANIF_00389]: See 7.20.\n[SWS_CANIF_00390]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf\naccepts an L-PDU received via\nCanIf_RxIndica-\ntion()\nduring Software Filtering (see [SWS_CANIF_00389]),\nCanIf\nshall process\nthe Data Length check afterwards, if configured (see\nCanIfPrivateData…"

   "chapter": 7,

   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P50_378",
   "page": 50,
   "text": "callback functions (see [SWS_CANIF_00012]) based on the parameters of\nCanIf_-\nRxIndication()\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_BSW_00325)\nNote: A single receive L-PDU can only be assigned to a single receive indication call-\nback service (refer to multiplicity of\nCanIfRxPduUserRxIndicationName\n).\nOverview: CanIf performs the following steps at a call of\nCanIf_RxIndication()\n:\n•\nSoftware Filtering (only BasicCAN), if configured\n•\nData Length Check, if configured\n•\nbuffer received\nL-SDU\nif configured\n•\ncall upper layer receive indication callback service, if configured.\n7.15 Read received data\nThe read received data API\nCanIf_ReadRxPduData()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00194])\nis a common interface for upper layer modules to read\nCAN L-SDUs\nrecently received\nfrom the CAN network. The upper layer modules initiate the receive request only via\nCanIf\nservices without direct access to\nCanDrv\n. The initiated receive request is suc-\ncessfully completed, if\nCanIf\nwrote the received\nL-SDU\ninto the upper layer module\nI-PDU buffer.\nThe function\nCanIf_ReadRxPduData()\nmakes reading out data without dependence\nof reception event (RxIndication) possible. When it is enabled at configuration time\n(see\nCanIfPublicReadRxPduDataApi\n), not necessarily a receive indication service\nfor the same\nL-SDU\nhas to be configured (see\nCanIfRxPduUserRxIndicationUL\n).\nIf needed, the receive indication can be enabled, too.\nBy this way the type of me…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P51_379",
   "page": 51,
   "text": "7.16 Read Tx/Rx notification status\nIn addition to the notification callback functions\nCanIf\nprovides the API service\nCanIf_ReadTxNotifStatus()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00202]) to read the transmit\nconfirmation status of any transmit\nL-SDU\nand the API service\nCanIf_ReadRxNo-\ntifStatus()\nis provided to read the receive indication status of any receive\nL-SDU\n.\nCanIf\n's API services\nCanIf_ReadTxNotifStatus()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00202])\nand\nCanIf_ReadRxNotifStatus()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00230]) can be en-\nabled/disabled globally or per\nL-SDU\nat pre-compile time configuration using the con-\nfiguration parameters\nCanIfPublicReadTxPduNotifyStatusApi\n,\nCanIfPubli-\ncReadRxPduNotifyStatusApi\n,\nCanIfTxPduReadNotifyStatus\n, and\nCanI-\nfRxPduReadNotifyStatus\n.\n[SWS_CANIF_00472]\n⌈\nIf configuration parameter\nCanIfPublicReadTxPduNoti-\nfyStatusApi\nis set to\nTRUE\n,\nCanIf\nshall store the current notification status for each\ntransmit\nL-SDU\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00473]\n⌈\nIf configuration parameter\nCanIfPublicReadRxPduNoti-\nfyStatusApi\nis set to\nTRUE\n,\nCanIf\nshall store the current notification status for each\nreceive\nL-SDU\n.\n⌋\n()\nRationale for [SWS_CANIF_00391] and [SWS_CANIF_00393] respectively\n[SWS_CANIF_00392] and [SWS_CANIF_00394]: This 'read-and-consume' be-\nhavior ensures, that at least one successful transmit or receive event occurred after\nlast call of this service.\n7.17 Data integrity\n[SWS_CANIF_00064] Shared c…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P53_381",
   "page": 53,
   "text": "7.18.2 CAN Controller Operation Modes\nAccording to the requested operation mode by\nCanSm\n,\nCanIf\nforwards request\nCan-\nDrvs\n.\n[SWS_CANIF_00677]\n⌈\nIf a controller mode referenced by\nControllerId\nis in state\nCAN_CS_STOPPED\nand if the\nPduIdType\nparameter in a call of\nCanIf_Transmit()\nis assigned to that\nCAN Controller\n, then the call of\nCanIf_Transmit()\ndoes not\nresult in a call of\nCan_Write()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00317]) and returns\nE_NOT_OK\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00485]\n⌈\nIf a controller mode referenced by\nControllerId\nenters state\nCAN_CS_STOPPED\n, then\nCanIf\nshall clear the CanIf transmit buffers assigned to the\nCAN Controller\ncorresponding.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00739]\n⌈\nIf a controller mode referenced by\nControllerId\nenters state\nCAN_CS_STOPPED\n, then\nCanIf\nshall inform corresponding upper layer modules about\nfailed transmission by calling\n<User_TxConfirmation>(id, E_NOT_OK)\nfor every\noutstanding TxConfirmation assigned to that CAN Controller. If\nCanIfPublicTx-\nConfirmPollingSupport\nis enabled,\nCanIf\nshall also clear the information about\na\nTxConfirmation\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00740]).\n⌋\n()\nNote: This ensures, that for each PDU, which shall be transmitted via\nCanIf_Trans-\nmit()\n, either a positive or negative\n<User_TxConfirmation>()\nis called.\n[SWS_CANIF_00724]\n⌈\nWhen callback\nCanIf_ControllerBusOff(Control-\nlerId)\nis called, the\nCanIf\nshall call\nCanSM_ControllerBusOff(Control-\nlerId)\nof the\nCanS…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P55_383",
   "page": 55,
   "text": "7.18.4.1 Wake-up detection\nIf\nwake-up support\nis enabled (see [SWS_CANIF_00180])\nCanIf\nis notified by the\nIntegration Code about a detected CAN wake-up by the service\nCanIf_CheckWakeup\n()\n(see CAN Wakeup Sequences of [13]).\nIn case of a CAN bus \"\nwake-up\n\" event the function\nCanIf_CheckWakeup(Wakeup-\nSource)\nmay be called during execution of\nEcuM_CheckWakeup(WakeupSource)\n(see wake-up sequence diagrams of\nEcuM\n).\nCanIf\nin turn checks by configured input\nreference to\nEcuMWakeupSource\nin\nCanDrvs\n, which\nCanDrvs\nhave to be checked.\nCanIf\ngets this information via reference\nCanIfCtrlCanCtrlRef\n.\nThe Communication Service, which is called, belongs to the service defined during\nconfiguration (see\nCanIfDispatchCfg\n). In this way\nEcuM\nas well as\nCanSm\nare able\nto change CAN Controller States and to control the system behavior concerning the\nBusOff recovery\nor\nwake-up procedure\n.\n[SWS_CANIF_00395]\n⌈\nWhen\nCanIf_CheckWakeup(EcuM_WakeupSourceType\nWakeupSource)\nis invoked,\nCanIf\nshall query\nCanDrvs\n/\nCanTrcvs\nvia\nCanTrcv_-\nCheckWakeup()\nor\nCan_CheckWakeup()\n, which exact CAN hardware device\ncaused the bus wake-up.\n⌋\n()\nNote: It is implementation specific, which controllers and transceivers are queried.\nCanIf\njust has to find out the exact CAN hardware device.\n[SWS_CANIF_00720]\n⌈\nIf at least one function call of\nCan_CheckWakeup()\nor\nCanTrcv_CheckWakeup()\nreturns\nE_OK\nto\nCanIf\n, then\nCanIf_C…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P56_384",
   "page": 56,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00226]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall provide wake-up service\nCanIf_CheckValida-\ntion()\nonly, if\n•\nunderlying\nCAN Controller\nprovides\nwake-up support\nand wake-up is enabled\nby the parameter\nCanIfCtrlWakeupSupport\nand by\nCanDrv\nconfiguration\n•\nand/or underlying\nCAN Transceiver\nprovides wake-up support and wake-up is\nenabled by the parameter\nCanIfTrcvWakeupSupport\nand by\nCanTrcv\ncon-\nfiguration\n•\nand configuration parameter\nCanIfPublicWakeupCheckValidSupport\nis\nenabled.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00286]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIfPublicWakeupCheckValidSupport\nequals\nTRUE\n,\nCanIf\nenables the detection for CAN wake-up validation. Therefore,\nCanIf\nstores the\nevent of the first valid call of\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nof a\nCAN Controller\nwhich\nhas been set to\nCAN_CS_STARTED\n. The first call of\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nis valid:\n•\nonly for received NM messages if\nCanIfPublicWakeupCheckValidByNM\nis\nTRUE\n•\nfor all received messages corresponding to a configured Rx PDU if\nCanIfPub-\nlicWakeupCheckValidByNM\nis\nFALSE\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01151)\n[SWS_CANIF_00179]\n⌈\n<User_ValidateWakeupEvent>(sources)\nshall be\ncalled during\nCanIf_CheckValidation(WakeupSource)\n, whereas\nsources\nis\nset to\nWakeupSource\n, if the event of the first called\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nis\nstored in\nCanIf\nat the corresponding\nCAN Controller\n.\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01136)\nNote: The parameter of the function\n<User_ValidateWakeupEvent>()\nis of type:\n•\nsources\n:\nEcuM_WakeupSourceType\n(see…"
  },

   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P57_385",
   "page": 57,
   "text": "Figure 7.7: Channel PDU groups\n7.19.2 PDU channel modes\nCanIf\nprovides the services\nCanIf_SetPduMode()\nand\nCanIf_GetPduMode()\nto\nprevent the processing of\n•\nall\nTransmit L-PDUs\nbelonging to one logical channel,\n•\nall\nTransmit L-PDUs\nand\nReceive L-PDUs\nbelonging to one logical channel.\nChanging the PDU channel mode is only allowed in case corresponding controller\nmode equals\nCAN_CS_STARTED\n(refer to [SWS_CANIF_00874])."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P58_387",
   "page": 58,
   "text": "Figure 7.8: PDU channel mode control\nFigure 7.8 shows a diagram with possible PDU channel modes. Each\nL-PDU\nchan-\nnel can be in\nCANIF_OFFLINE\n(no communication),\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE\n(passive\nmode => listen without sending),\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE\n(simulated transmis-\nsion without listening (see [SWS_CANIF_00072]), and\nCANIF_ONLINE\n(full communi-\ncation). The default state is the\nCANIF_OFFLINE\nmode.\n7.19.2.1 CANIF_OFFLINE\n[SWS_CANIF_00864]\n⌈\nDuring initialization\nCanIf\nshall switch every channel to\nCANIF_OFFLINE\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00865]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_SetControllerMode(ControllerId, CAN_-\nCS_SLEEP)\nis called,\nCanIf\nshall set the PDU channel mode of the corresponding\nchannel to\nCANIF_OFFLINE\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00073]\n⌈\nFor\nPhysical Channels\nswitching to\nCANIF_OFFLINE\nmode\nCanIf\nshall:\n•\nprevent forwarding of transmit requests\nCanIf_Transmit()\nof associated\nL-PDUs\nto\nCanDrv\n(return\nE_NOT_OK\nto the calling upper layer modules),\n•\nclear the corresponding\nCanIf\ntransmit buffers,\n•\nprevent invocation of receive indication callback services of the upper layer mod-\nules,"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P59_388",
   "page": 59,
   "text": "•\nprevent invocation of transmit confirmation callback services of the upper layer\nmodules.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00866]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_SetControllerMode(ControllerId, CAN_-\nCS_STOPPED)\nor\nCanIf_ControllerBusOff(ControllerId)\nis called,\nCanIf\nshall set the PDU channel mode of the corresponding channel to\nCANIF_TX_OF-\nFLINE\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00489]\n⌈\nFor\nPhysical Channels\nswitching to\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE\nmode\nCanIf\nshall:\n•\nprevent forwarding of transmit requests\nCanIf_Transmit()\nof associated\nL-PDUs\nto\nCanDrv\n(return\nE_NOT_OK\nto the calling upper layer modules),\n•\nclear the corresponding CanIf transmit buffers,\n•\nprevent invocation of transmit confirmation callback services of the upper layer\nmodules.\n•\nenable invocation of receive indication callback services of the upper layer mod-\nules.\n⌋\n()\nThe\nBusOff\nnotification is implicitly suppressed in case of\nCANIF_OFFLINE\nand\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE\ndue to the fact, that no\nL-PDUs\ncan be transmitted and thus\nthe\nCAN Controller\nis not able to go in\nBusOff\nmode by newly requested\nL-PDUs\nfor transmission.\n[SWS_CANIF_00118]\n⌈\nIf those\nTransmit L-PDUs\n, which are already waiting for\ntransmission in the\nCAN Transmit Hardware Object\n, will be transmitted imme-\ndiately after change to\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE\nor\nCANIF_OFFLINE\nmode and a subse-\nquent\nBusOff\nevent occurs,\nCanIf\ndoes not prohibit execution of the\nBusOff\nnotifica-\ntion\n<User_ControllerBusOff>(ControllerI…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P60_389",
   "page": 60,
   "text": "•\nenable invocation of transmit confirmation callback services of the upper layer\nmodules.\n⌋\n()\n7.19.2.3 CANIF_OFFLINE_ACTIVE\nIf\nCanIfTxOfflineActiveSupport = TRUE CanIf\nprovides simulation of suc-\ncessful transmission by\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE\nmode. This mode is enabled\nby call of\nCanIf_SetPduMode(ControllerId, CANIF_TX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE)\nand only affects the transmission path.\n[SWS_CANIF_00072]\n⌈\nFor every\nL-PDU\nassigned to a channel which is in\nCANIF_-\nTX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE\nmode\nCanIf\nshall call the transmit confirmation callback ser-\nvices of the upper layer modules immediately instead of buffering or forwarding of the\nL-PDUs\nto\nCanDrv\nduring the call of\nCanIf_Transmit()\n.\n⌋\n()\nNote: During\nCANIF_TX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE\nmode the upper layer has to handle the\nexecution of the transmit confirmations. The transmit confirmation handling is executed\nimmediately at the end of the transmit request (see [SWS_CANIF_00072]).\nRational: This functionality is useful to realize special operating modes (i.e. diagnosis\npassive mode) to avoid bus traffic without impact to the notification mechanism. This\nmode is typically used for diagnostic usage.\n7.20 Software receive filter\nNot all\nL-PDUs\n, which may pass the hardware acceptance filter and therefore are\nsuccessful received in\nBasicCAN\nHardware Objects\n, are defined as\nReceive\nL-PDUs\nand thus needed from the corresponding ECU.\nCanIf\noptionally filte…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P61_390",
   "page": 61,
   "text": "•\na list of\nReceive L-PDUs\nor\n•\none or multiple ranges of\nReceive L-PDUs\ncan be linked to a\nHardware Re-\nceive Object\n(\nBasicCAN\nreception).\nFor definition of range reception it is necessary to define at least one\nRx L-PDU\nwhere\nthe\nCanId\nor the complete ID range is inside the defined range.\n[SWS_CANIF_00645]\n⌈\nA range of\nCanIds\nwhich shall pass the software receive filter\nshall either be defined by its upper limit (see\nCanIfHrhRangeRxPduUpperCanId\n)\nand lower limit (see\nCanIfHrhRangeRxPduLowerCanId\n)\nCanId\n, or by a base ID\n(see\nCanIfHrhRangeBaseId\n) and a mask that defines the relevant bits of the base\nID (see\nCanIfHrhRangeMask\n).\n⌋\n()\nNote: Software receive filtering is optional (see multiplicity of\n0\n::\n\u0003\nin\nCan-\nIfHrhRangeCfg\n).\n[SWS_CANIF_00646]\n⌈\nEach configurable range of\nCanIds\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00645]), which shall pass the software receive filter, shall\nbe configurable either for\nStandard CAN IDs\nor\nExtended CAN IDs\nvia\nCan-\nIfHrhRangeRxPduRangeCanIdType\n.\n⌋\n()\nReceive L-PDUs\nare provided as constant structures statically generated from the\ncommunication matrix. They are arranged according to the corresponding hardware\nacceptance filter, so that there is one single list of receive\nCanIds\nfor every\nHardware\nReceive Object\n(\nHRH\n). The corresponding list can be derived by the\nHRH\n, if multiple\nBasicCAN\nobjects are used. The subsequent filtering is the search through one…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P61_391",
   "page": 61,
   "text": "Figure 7.9: Software filtering example\n[SWS_CANIF_00852]\n⌈\nIf a range is (partly) contained in another range, or a single\nCanId\nis contained in a range, the software filter shall select the\nL-PDU\nbased on the\nfollowing assumptions:\n•\nA single\nCanId\nis always more relevant than a range."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P62_392",
   "page": 62,
   "text": "•\nA smaller range is more relevant than a larger range.\n⌋\n()\n7.20.2 Software filter algorithms\nThe choice of suitable software search algorithms it is up to the implementation of\nCanIf\n. According to the wide range of possible receive\nBasicCAN\noperations provided\nby the\nCAN Controller\nit is recommended to offer several search algorithms like\nlinear search, table search and/or hash search variants to provide the most optimal\nsolution for most use cases.\n7.21 Data Length Check\nThe received Data Length value is compared with the configured Data Length value\nof the received L-PDU. The configured Data Length value shall be derived from the\nsize of used bytes inside this L-PDU. The configured Data Length value may not be\nnecessarily that Data Length value defined in the CAN communication matrix and used\nby the sender of this CAN L-PDU.\n[SWS_CANIF_00026]\n⌈\nCanIf\nshall accept all received L-PDUs\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00390]) with a Data Length value equal or greater then the\nconfigured Data Length value (see\nCanIfRxPduDataLength\n).\n⌋\n(SRS_Can_01005)\n[SWS_CANIF_00902]\n⌈\nThe Data Length Check shall be processed if it is enabled\nglobally (see\nCanIfPrivateDataLengthCheck\n) and not disabled individually per\nPDU (see\nCanIfRxPduDataLengthCheck\n).\n⌋\n()\nHint: If the Data Length Check is disabled globally, it can't be enabled individually per\nPDU.\n[SWS_CANIF_00168]\n⌈\nIf the Data Length Check rejects…"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P64_394",
   "page": 64,
   "text": "CanDrv\nfrom the\nL-SDU\npassed in the APIs. The parameters have to be translated\naccordingly: i.e. L-SDU => HTH/HRH, CanId, Data Length.\"\nThe support for multiple\nCanDrvs\ncan be enabled and disabled by the configuration\nparameter\nCanIfPublicMultipleDrvSupport\n.\n7.24.1 Transmit requests by using multiple CAN Drivers\nEach\nTransmit L-PDU\nenables\nCanIf\nto derive the corresponding\nCAN Con-\ntroller\nand implicitly\nCanDrv\nserving the affected\nHardware Unit\n. Resolving of\nthese dependencies is possible because of the construction of the\nCAN Controller\nHandle\n: it combines\nCanDrv Handle\nand the corresponding\nCAN Controller\nin the\nHardware Unit\n.\nAt configuration time a\nCAN Controller Handle\nwill be mapped to each\nCAN Con-\ntroller\n. The sequence diagram Figure 7.10 below demonstrates two transmit re-\nquests directed to different\nCanDrvs\n.\nCanIf\nneeds only to select the corresponding\nCanDrv\nin order to call the correct API service.\nNote: Figure 7.10 and the following table serve only as an example. Finally, it is up to\nthe implementation to access the correct APIs of underlying\nCanDrvs\n."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": true,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P66_397",
   "page": 66,
   "text": "Figure 7.11: Receive interrupt with multiple\nCanDrvs\n- simplified"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P67_408",
   "page": 67,
   "text": "7.25 Partial Networking\n[SWS_CANIF_00747]\n⌈\nIf\nPartial Networking\n(PN) is enabled (see\nCanIfPublicPn-\nSupport\n),\nCanIf\nshall support a\nPnTxFilter\nper\nCAN Controller\nwhich overlays\nthe\nPDU channel modes\n.\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00748]\n⌈\nThe\nPnTxFilter\nof [SWS_CANIF_00747] shall only have\nan effect and transition its modes (enabled/disabled) if more than zero\nTx L-PDUs\nper\nCAN Controller\nare configured as\nCanIfTxPduPnFilterPdu\n(see\nCanIfTx-\nPduPnFilterPdu\n).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00863]\n⌈\nPnTxFilter\nshall be enabled during initialization (ref. to\n[SWS_CANIF_00747] and [SWS_CANIF_00748]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00749]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_SetControllerMode(ControllerId, CAN_-\nCS_SLEEP)\nis called the\nPnTxFilter\nof the corresponding\nCAN Controller\nshall\nbe enabled (ref. to [SWS_CANIF_00748] and [SWS_CANIF_00747]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00750]\n⌈\nIf the\nPnTxFilter\nof a\nCAN Controller\nis enabled,\nCanIf\nshall block all Tx requests to that\nCAN Controller\n(return\nE_NOT_OK\nwhen\nCanIf_-\nTransmit()\nis called), except if the requested\nTx L-PDUs\nis one of the configured\nCanIfTxPduPnFilterPdus\nof that\nCAN Controller\n. These\nCanIfTxPduPnFil-\nterPdus\nshall always be passed to the corresponding\nCAN Driver\n.\n⌋\n()"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P68_409",
   "page": 68,
   "text": "[SWS_CANIF_00751]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_TxConfirmation()\nis called, the corre-\nsponding\nPnTxFilter\nshall be disabled (ref. to [SWS_CANIF_00747] and\n[SWS_CANIF_00748]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00896]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_RxIndication()\nis called and PnTxFilter is en-\nabled, the corresponding\nPnTxFilter\nshall be disabled (ref. to [SWS_CANIF_00747]\nand [SWS_CANIF_00748]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00752]\n⌈\nIf the\nPnTxFilter\nof a\nCAN Controller\nis disabled,\nCanIf\nshall behave as requested via\nCanIf_SetPduMode()\n(see [SWS_CANIF_00008]).\n⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00878]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_SetPduMode(ControllerId, CANIF_TX_OF-\nFLINE)\nis called and Partial Networking is enabled (ref. to\nCanIfPublicPnSup-\nport\n) the\nPnTxFilter\nof the corresponding\nCAN Controller\nshall be enabled (ref.\nto [SWS_CANIF_00748] and [SWS_CANIF_00747]).\n⌋\n()\n7.26 CAN FD Support\nFor performance reasons some\nCAN Controllers\nallow to use a Flexible Data-Rate\nfeature called\nCAN FD\n(see [12, ISO 11898-1:2015]). Besides, the higher baud rate for\nthe payload\nCAN FD\nalso supports an extended payload which allows the transmission\nof up to 64 bytes. If these features are available depends on the general\nCAN FD\nsupport by the\nCAN Controller\nand if the\nCAN Controller\nis in\nCAN FD\nmode\n(valid\nCanControllerFdBaudrateConfig\n).\nIf an\nL-SDU\nshall be sent as\nCAN FD\nor conventional CAN 2.0 frame depends on\nthe configured\nCanIfTxPduCanIdType\n.\nCanIf\nindicates this to\nCanDrv\nutilizing\nt…"
  },

   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P69_410",
   "page": 69,
   "text": "system point of view, the format for each frame has to be configured. Otherwise the\nsender wouldn't know which kind of frame shall be transmitted.\n7.27 Security Events\n[SWS_CANIF_91010] Security events for CanIf\n⌈"
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P69_411",
   "page": 69,
   "text": "⌋\n()\n[SWS_CANIF_00913]\n⌈\nIf security event reporting has been enabled for the\nCanIf\nmodule (\nCanIfEnableSecurityEventReporting\n= true) the respective security\nevents shall bereported to the IdsM via the interfaces defined in\nAUTOSAR_SWS_-\nBSWGeneral\n.\n⌋\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_CANIF_00915]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_ErrorNotification()\nis called by\nCanDrv\n, the\nfunction shall evaluate whether a Tx related error was detected. If this is the case the\nCanIf\nshall report the security event CANIF_SEV_TX_ERROR_DETECTED.\nThe context data is structured as follows:\nContext Data (2 Byte)\n•\nControllerID (1 Byte)\n•\nCanError (1 Byte)\n\nCAN_ERROR_BIT_MONITORING1 (0x1)\n\nCAN_ERROR_BIT_MONITORING0 (0x2)\n\nCAN_ERROR_BIT (0x3)\n\nCAN_ERROR_CHECK_ACK_FAILED (0x4)\n\nCAN_ERROR_ACK_DELIMITER (0x5)\n\nCAN_ERROR_ARBITRATION_LOST (0x6)\n\nCAN_ERROR_OVERLOAD (0x7)\n⌋\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_CANIF_00916]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_ErrorNotification()\nis called by\nCanDrv\n, the\nfunction shall evaluate whether a Rx related error was detected. If this is the case the\nCanIf\nshall report the security event\nCANIF_SEV_RX_ERROR_DETECTED\n."
  },
  {
   "chapter": 7,
   "doc": "AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface",
   "figure": false,
   "id": "SNIP_Can_AUTOSAR_SWS_CANI_P70_412",
   "page": 70,
   "text": "The context data is structured as follows:\nContext Data (2 Byte)\n•\nControllerID (1 Byte)\n•\nCanError (1 Byte)\n\nCAN_ERROR_CHECK_FORM_FAILED (0x8)\n\nCAN_ERROR_CHECK_STUFFING_FAILED (0x9)\n\nCAN_ERROR_CHECK_CRC_FAILED (0xA)\n\nCAN_ERROR_BUS_LOCK (0xB)\n⌋\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_CANIF_00917]\n⌈\nIf\nCanIf_ControllerErrorStatePassive()\nis called by\nCanDrv\n, the\nCanIf\nshall report the security event\nCANIF_SEV_ERRORSTATE_PAS-\nSIVE\nin following cases:\n•\nTxErrorCounter > 127 and TxErrorCounter <= 255\n•\nRxErrorCounter > 127 and TxErrorCounter <= 255\nThe context data is structured as follows:\nContext Data (2 Byte)\n•\nControllerID (1 Byte)\n•\nErrorCounterThreshold (1 Byte)\n\nTxErrorCounter > 127 AND RxErrorCounter > 127(0x0)\n\nTxErrorCounter > 127 AND RxErrorCounter < 127 (0x1)\n\nRxErrorCounter > 127 AND TxErrorCounter < 127 (0x2)\n⌋\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n[SWS_CANIF_00918]\n⌈\nIf CanIf_ControllerBusOff is called by\nCanDrv\n, the\nCanIf\nshall\nreport the security event\nCANIF_SEV_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF\n. The context data is\nstructured as follows:\nContext Data (1 Byte)\n•\nController ID (1 Byte)\n⌋\n(RS_Ids_00810)\n7.28 Error classification\n[SWS_CANIF_00223]\n⌈\nFor all defined production errors it is only required to report\nthe event, when an error or diagnostic relevant event (e.g. state changes, no L-PDU\nevents) occurs. Any status has not to be reported.\n⌋\n()"

   "id": "SWS_Can_91010",
   "text": ". Specification of CAN Driver AUTOSAR CP R20 - 11 34 of 112 Document ID 11 : AUTOSAR_SWS_CANDriver 7.3 CAN Controller State Machine Each CAN controller has complex state machines impleme nted in hardware. For simplification, the number of states is reduced to the following four basic states in this description: UNINIT, STOPPED, STARTED and SLEEP. Any CAN hardware access is encapsulated by functions of the Can module, but the Can module doe s not memorize the state changes. The Can module offers t he services Can_Init, Can_Set Baudrate and Can_SetControllerMode. These services perform the nece…"

  <h4>Systemgrenzen und Einbettung des CAN-Treibers</h4>
  <p>
    Das Classic-AUTOSAR-Modul <code>Can</code> (CAN-Treiber / CanDrv) bildet die hardwarenächste Schicht des CAN-Kommunikationsstacks und kapselt die hardwarespezifischen Eigenschaften der CAN-Controller sowie deren Register und Mailboxen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00413" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00413">[SWS_Can_00413]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>). Es stellt der darüberliegenden Schnittstelle <code>CanIf</code> (CAN Interface) eine hardwareunabhängige, standardisierte Programmierschnittstelle zur Verfügung, sodass übergeordnete Protokollinstanzen wie PduR, CanNm oder CanTp ohne Anpassungen an Mikrocontroller-Spezifika betrieben werden können (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=11">CAN-Interface §1.1 „AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=20">CAN-Interface §5 „Hardware-Unabhängigkeit und Callbacks“</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Eine physische CAN-Hardware-Einheit (CAN Hardware Unit) fasst dabei einen oder mehrere CAN-Controller gleichen Typs zusammen, die entweder auf dem Halbleiterchip integriert oder als externe Standalone-Bausteine angebunden sind (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=36">CAN-Interface §7.6 „CAN Hardware Unit“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=37">CAN-Interface §7.6 „Typical CAN Hardware Unit“</a>). Werden in einem Steuergerät mehrere unterschiedliche Controllertypen parallel eingesetzt, bedient jeweils eine spezifische Instanz des CAN-Treibers die entsprechende Hardware-Einheit, während <code>CanIf</code> über Funktionszeiger zur Link-Zeit auf die Treiber-APIs zugreift (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=22">CAN-Interface §5.7.1 „Code file structure“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=64">CAN-Interface §7.24.1 „Transmit requests by using multiple CAN Drivers“</a>).
  </p>

  <p class="diagram-note">Kontextdiagramm: Einbettung des CAN-Treibers zwischen BSW-Modulen und den physischen CAN-Controllern. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=11">CAN-Interface §1.1 „AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=36">CAN-Interface §7.6 „CAN Hardware Unit“</a></p>

  <h4>Initialisierung und Betriebsmodi der CAN-Controller</h4>
  <p>
    Der Lebenszyklus des Treibers beginnt in der Startphase des Gesamtsystems: Der ECU State Manager (EcuM) ruft synchron die Funktion <code>Can_Init</code> auf und übergibt dabei den Zeiger auf die treiberweite Konfigurationsstruktur <code>Can_ConfigType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00413" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00413">[SWS_Can_00413]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>). Hierbei initialisiert der Treiber statische Variablen, globale Register der CAN-Hardware-Einheit sowie controllerspezifische Parameter, verbleibt jedoch bezüglich der Netzwerkkommunikation in einem inaktiven Grundzustand (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=39">CAN-Interface §7.8 „Initialization“</a>). Das Gegenstück zur Initialisierung bildet <code>Can_DeInit</code>, welches die Baugruppe wieder in den Ausgangszustand zurückversetzt (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Die Spezifikation abstrahiert die komplexen mikrocontrollerspezifischen Zustandsmaschinen der CAN-Hardware auf vier elementare Zustände des Aufzählungstyps <code>Can_ControllerStateType</code>: <code>CAN_CS_UNINIT</code>, <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code>, <code>CAN_CS_STARTED</code> und <code>CAN_CS_SLEEP</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>). Unmittelbar nach erfolgreicher Ausführung von <code>Can_Init</code> befinden sich alle Controller im Modus <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code>, in welchem weder das Senden noch das Empfangen von Nachrichten auf dem Bus möglich ist (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=39">CAN-Interface §7.8 „Initialization“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „CAN Controller Operation Modes“</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Zustandsübergänge werden asynchron durch die übergeordnete Schicht mittels <code>Can_SetControllerMode</code> angefordert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>). Der Treiber speichert die Zustände der Controller nicht eigenständig persistent als Softwarespeicher, sondern führt die Hardwareübergänge durch und meldet die vollzogene Transition über das Callback <code>CanIf_ControllerModeIndication</code> an das <code>CanIf</code> zurück (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>). Ergänzend kann der aktuelle Zustand jederzeit synchron über <code>Can_GetControllerMode</code> abgefragt werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91014">[SWS_Can_91014]</a>).
  </p>
