Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a></p>

  <h4>Sende- und Empfangsarchitektur über Hardware-Objekte</h4>
  <p>
    Die Kopplung zwischen den logischen Kommunikationspuffern der oberen Schichten und den konkreten Hardware-Mailboxen des CAN-Controllers erfolgt über abstrakte Bezeichner, die sogenannten Hardware Object Handles (HOH) vom Typ <code>Can_HwHandleType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00429" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00429">[SWS_Can_00429]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=29">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Hardware object handles“</a>). Dabei wird unterschieden zwischen Sende-Handles (Hardware Transmit Handles, HTH) und Empfangs-Handles (Hardware Receive Handles, HRH) (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=29">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Hardware object handles“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=31">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Definition of HTH“</a>). Innerhalb einer Hardware-Einheit bilden sämtliche HOHs einen zusammenhängenden Nummerierungsbereich beginnend bei null (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=31">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Numbering area starting with zero“</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Zur Übertragung einer Nachricht übergibt <code>CanIf</code> dem Treiber über den synchronen Dienst <code>Can_Write</code> das Ziel-HTH sowie einen Zeiger auf die Datenstruktur <code>Can_PduType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=41">CAN-Interface §7.10 „Transmit data flow“</a>). Diese Struktur bündelt das Software-PDU-Handle (<code>swPduHandle</code>), die Nutzlänge (<code>length</code>), die Nutzdaten (<code>sdu</code>) sowie den CAN-Identifier (<code>id</code> vom Typ <code>Can_IdType</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00416" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00416">[SWS_Can_00416]</a>). Die zwei höchstwertigen Bits von <code>Can_IdType</code> kennzeichnen dabei das Frame-Format: Standard-CAN, Extended-CAN sowie deren jeweilige CAN-FD-Pendants (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00416" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00416">[SWS_Can_00416]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=33">CAN-Interface §7.4.1 „Dynamic Transmit L-PDUs“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=68">CAN-Interface §7.26 „CAN FD Support“</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Ist im Controller keine freie Sende-Mailbox verfügbar, weist der Treiber die Übertragungsanforderung ab und liefert den speziellen Statuswert <code>CAN_BUSY</code> (Wert 0x02) zurück (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=40">CAN-Interface §7.9 „Transmit request“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=43">CAN-Interface §7.11.2.1 „Storage of L-PDUs in the transmit L-PDU buffer“</a>). In diesem Fall obliegt es der Software-Pufferung im <code>CanIf</code>, die Nachricht zwischenzuspeichern und erneut zu übermitteln, sobald eine Mailbox frei wird (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=42">CAN-Interface §7.11.1 „General behavior“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=45">CAN-Interface §7.11.2.1 „Priority order“</a>). Sobald der Frame erfolgreich über das Netz versendet wurde, informiert der Treiber das <code>CanIf</code> via <code>CanIf_TxConfirmation</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=46">CAN-Interface §7.12 „Transmit confirmation“</a>).
  </p>

  <p class="diagram-note">Sequenzdiagramm: Ablauf einer Sendeanforderung mit Pufferung und Bestätigung. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=41">CAN-Interface §7.10 „Transmit data flow“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=46">CAN-Interface §7.12 „Transmit confirmation“</a></p>
  <p>
    Im Empfangspfad werden eingehende Nachrichten hardwareseitig über HRHs erfasst. Die Architektur unterscheidet zwischen FullCAN-Objekten, die jeweils nur für eine einzelne feste CAN-ID konfiguriert sind, und BasicCAN-Objekten, die über Hardware-Filter ganze ID-Bereiche empfangen (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=37">CAN-Interface §7.7 „BasicCAN and FullCAN reception“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=38">CAN-Interface §7.7 „Hardware acceptance filter“</a>). Vor der Übergabe der empfangenen Daten an das <code>CanIf</code> via <code>CanIf_RxIndication</code> kann optional eine konfigurierte LPDU-Callout-Funktion ausgeführt werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00443" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00443">[SWS_Can_00443]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=47">CAN-Interface §7.13 „Receive data flow“</a>). Diese Callout-Funktion prüft die Frame-Daten auf Treiberebene; liefert sie <code>false</code>, wird die Weiterleitung abgebrochen, womit unzulässige oder irrelevante Frames frühzeitig gefiltert werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00443" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00443">[SWS_Can_00443]</a>).
  </p>

  <p class="diagram-note">Aktivitätsdiagramm: Empfangsverarbeitung von CAN-Frames auf Treiberebene inklusive Callout-Entscheidung. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00443" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00443">[SWS_Can_00443]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=47">CAN-Interface §7.13 „Receive data flow“</a></p>

  <h4>Ereignisverarbeitung: Polling versus Interrupts</h4>
  <p>
    Zur Entkopplung von Busereignissen unterstützt der CAN-Treiber sowohl interruptgetriebene als auch zyklisch gepolte Betriebsarten. Für zeitkritische Abschnitte oder zur Realisierung von exklusiven Bereichen können die Controller-Interrupts synchron über <code>Can_DisableControllerInterrupts</code> gesperrt und über <code>Can_EnableControllerInterrupts</code> wieder freigegeben werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00231" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00231">[SWS_Can_00231]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00232" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00232">[SWS_Can_00232]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Wird ein Kanal oder Ereignistyp im Polling-Modus betrieben, ruft der BSW-Scheduler (SchM) zyklisch die spezifischen Main-Functions des Moduls auf (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00225" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00225">[SWS_Can_00225]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00226" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00226">[SWS_Can_00226]</a>). Hierzu zählen <code>Can_MainFunction_Write</code> zur Abfrage getätigter Sendeübertragungen, <code>Can_MainFunction_Read</code> zur Bearbeitung empfangener Nachrichten, <code>Can_MainFunction_BusOff</code> zur Erkennung von Bus-Off-Zuständen, <code>Can_MainFunction_Wakeup</code> zur Erfassung von Weckereignissen sowie <code>Can_MainFunction_Mode</code> zur Überwachung von asynchronen Zustandsübergängen der Controller (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00225" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00225">[SWS_Can_00225]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00226" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00226">[SWS_Can_00226]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00227" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00227">[SWS_Can_00227]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00228" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00228">[SWS_Can_00228]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00368" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00368">[SWS_Can_00368]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Im Weck- und Standby-Szenario dient die API <code>Can_CheckWakeup</code> der Überprüfung, ob ein spezifizierter Controller das Weckereignis des Steuergeräts ausgelöst hat (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00360" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00360">[SWS_Can_00360]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=55">CAN-Interface §7.18.4.1 „Wake-up detection“</a>). Dieses Verfahren ermöglicht es dem System, schlafende Controller gezielt zu identifizieren und den Kommunikationsstack bedarfsgerecht wieder in Betrieb zu nehmen (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=55">CAN-Interface §7.18.4.1 „Wake-up detection“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=56">CAN-Interface §7.18.4.1 „Wake-up validation“</a>).
  </p>

  <h4>Partitionierung und Mehrkernunterstützung</h4>
  <p>
    In modernen Steuergerätearchitekturen mit Multicore- und Sicherheitszonen-Aufteilung unterliegt der CAN-Treiber strengen Randbedingungen bezüglich der Speicher- und Partitionszuordnung. Gemäß <code>SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508</code> agiert das Modul in jeder ECUC-Partition als eigenständige Instanz, sodass API-Aufrufe stets nur die Ressourcen und Datenstrukturen derjenigen Partition betreffen, aus der heraus sie aufgerufen wurden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Die Konfigurationskonsistenz wird durch komplementäre Constraints abgesichert: Die durch <code>CanControllerEcucPartitionRef</code> referenzierten Partitionen müssen eine echte Teilmenge der globalen Treiber-Partitionsreferenzen (<code>CanEcucPartitionRef</code>) darstellen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509]</a>). Zudem müssen der CAN-Controller und der zugehörige Transceiver-Kanal eines physischen Kommunikationskanals zwingend dieselbe Partition referenzieren (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510]</a>). Konfigurationen mit Partitionszuordnungen, die von der jeweiligen Hardware- oder Software-Implementierung nicht unterstützt werden, weist das Modul strikt zurück (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00507" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00507">[SWS_Can_00507]</a>).
  </p>

  <h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
  <p>
    Der CAN-Treiber unterscheidet zwischen Fehlern im Software-Ablauf (Entwicklungs- und Laufzeitfehler) und Fehlern auf der physischen Bitebene des CAN-Busses (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>). Wird eine API mit ungültigen Zeigern aufgerufen, meldet der Treiber <code>CAN_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>). Fehlerhafte Handle-, Längen- oder Controller-Parameter führen zu <code>CAN_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code>, <code>CAN_E_PARAM_DATA_LENGTH</code> beziehungsweise <code>CAN_E_PARAM_CONTROLLER</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>). Der Aufruf von Diensten vor der Initialisierung wird über <code>CAN_E_UNINIT</code> signalisiert, unzulässige Moduswechsel lösen <code>CAN_E_TRANSITION</code> aus und fehlerhafte Baudrateneinstellungen werden mit <code>CAN_E_PARAM_BAUDRATE</code> quittiert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>). Ein Verlust empfangener Nachrichten durch Pufferüberlauf in der Hardware wird als Laufzeitfehler <code>CAN_E_DATALOST</code> erfasst (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91020">[SWS_Can_91020]</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Zur Diagnose des Controller-Zustands auf dem Netzwerk stellt der Treiber Statusabfragen bereit. Über den Dienst <code>Can_GetControllerErrorState</code> lässt sich der aktuelle Fehlerstatus (<code>Can_ErrorStateType</code>) auslesen, welcher die Zustände <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_ACTIVE</code>, <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_PASSIVE</code> und <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF</code> umfasst (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a>). Während der Controller im aktiven Zustand vollwertig an der Kommunikation teilnimmt und aktive Error-Frames aussendet, sendet er im Zustand <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_PASSIVE</code> lediglich passive Fehlersignale; im Zustand <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF</code> ist er vollständig vom Bus isoliert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „CAN Controller Operation Modes“</a>).
  </p>
  <p>
    Über die APIs <code>Can_GetControllerRxErrorCounter</code> und <code>Can_GetControllerTxErrorCounter</code> können die internen Hardware-Fehlerzähler (REC und TEC) gezielt abgefragt werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>). Überschreitet der Sende-Fehlerzähler den Schwellwert zur Bus-Off-Kondition, meldet der Treiber dieses gravierende Ereignis über den Callback <code>CanIf_ControllerBusOff</code> an das <code>CanIf</code>, welches in der Folge das Zustandsmanagement (CanSM) und die PDU-Kanalmodi koordiniert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „BusOff-Benachrichtigung“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=59">CAN-Interface §7.19.2.1 „CANIF_TX_OFFLINE bei BusOff“</a>). Zudem werden detaillierte Bit- und Protokollfehler wie Bit-Monitoring-, Acknowledge-, CRC- oder Stuffing-Fehler über den Typ <code>Can_ErrorType</code> klassifiziert und für Sicherheits- sowie Diagnosemechanismen bereitgestellt (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=69">CAN-Interface §7.27 „Security Events“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=70">CAN-Interface §7.27 „Security Events für Controller-Zustände“</a>).
  </p>

Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00227" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00227">[SWS_Can_00227]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a></p>

  <h4>Weiterführende Detailbelege</h4>
  <p>
    Zur vertiefenden Betrachtung der Modulschnittstellen und Konfigurationsmechanismen dienen die folgenden Kernanforderungen und Dokumentstellen der AUTOSAR-Spezifikation:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <strong>Modulinitialisierung und Konfiguration:</strong> Die strukturierte Bereitstellung der Konfigurationsdaten erfolgt über <code>Can_ConfigType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00413" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00413">[SWS_Can_00413]</a>), ausgeführt durch <code>Can_Init</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>) und rückgebaut via <code>Can_DeInit</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a>). Versionsinformationen liefert <code>Can_GetVersionInfo</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00224" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00224">[SWS_Can_00224]</a>).
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Controller-Zustandsverwaltung:</strong> Die Definitionen der Controller-Betriebszustände finden sich in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>; deren Steuerung erfolgt über <code>Can_SetControllerMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>) und <code>Can_GetControllerMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91014">[SWS_Can_91014]</a>) im Zusammenspiel mit <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „CAN Controller Operation Modes“</a>.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Datenübertragung und Hardware-Abstraktion:</strong> Sende- und Empfangsobjekte basieren auf <code>Can_HwHandleType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00429" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00429">[SWS_Can_00429]</a>) und den PDU-Definitionen in <code>Can_PduType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>) sowie <code>Can_IdType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00416" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00416">[SWS_Can_00416]</a>). Die Übermittlung steuert <code>Can_Write</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>) unter Berücksichtigung des Rückgabewerts <code>CAN_BUSY</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>) und Callbacks wie <code>CanIf_TxConfirmation</code> und <code>CanIf_RxIndication</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=20">CAN-Interface §5 „Hardware-Unabhängigkeit und Callbacks“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=41">CAN-Interface §7.10 „Transmit data flow“</a>).
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Fehlerbehandlung und Busüberwachung:</strong> Die Klassifizierung von Entwicklungsfehlern wird in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a> geregelt, Datenverlust in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91020">[SWS_Can_91020]</a>. Der Hardware-Fehlerstatus wird über <code>Can_ErrorStateType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>) und <code>Can_GetControllerErrorState</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a>) zusammen mit den Fehlerzählern (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>) und Protokollfehlertypen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>) ermittelt.
    </li>
    <li>
      <strong>Multicore- und Partitions-Constraints:</strong> Die partitionsbezogene Instanziierung und Referenzintegrität ist normiert durch die Festlegungen in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510]</a> sowie <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00507" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00507">[SWS_Can_00507]</a>.
    </li>
  </ul>
  <p class="ai-note">Dieser Modul-Leitfaden wurde auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikationen für das Release R20-11 maschinell generiert.</p>

The original reference version is shown below.</div> <h4>Systemgrenzen und Einbettung des CAN-Treibers</h4> <p> Das Classic-AUTOSAR-Modul <code>Can</code> (CAN-Treiber / CanDrv) bildet die hardwarenächste Schicht des CAN-Kommunikationsstacks und kapselt die hardwarespezifischen Eigenschaften der CAN-Controller sowie deren Register und Mailboxen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00413" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00413">[SWS_Can_00413]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>). Es stellt der darüberliegenden Schnittstelle <code>CanIf</code> (CAN Interface) eine hardwareunabhängige, standardisierte Programmierschnittstelle zur Verfügung, sodass übergeordnete Protokollinstanzen wie PduR, CanNm oder CanTp ohne Anpassungen an Mikrocontroller-Spezifika betrieben werden können (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=11">CAN-Interface §1.1 „AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=20">CAN-Interface §5 „Hardware-Unabhängigkeit und Callbacks“</a>). </p> <p> Eine physische CAN-Hardware-Einheit (CAN Hardware Unit) fasst dabei einen oder mehrere CAN-Controller gleichen Typs zusammen, die entweder auf dem Halbleiterchip integriert oder als externe Standalone-Bausteine angebunden sind (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=36">CAN-Interface §7.6 „CAN Hardware Unit“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=37">CAN-Interface §7.6 „Typical CAN Hardware Unit“</a>). Werden in einem Steuergerät mehrere unterschiedliche Controllertypen parallel eingesetzt, bedient jeweils eine spezifische Instanz des CAN-Treibers die entsprechende Hardware-Einheit, während <code>CanIf</code> über Funktionszeiger zur Link-Zeit auf die Treiber-APIs zugreift (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=22">CAN-Interface §5.7.1 „Code file structure“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=64">CAN-Interface §7.24.1 „Transmit requests by using multiple CAN Drivers“</a>). </p> <div class="diagram" Frames</text> </g> </g> </svg></div> <p class="diagram-note">Kontextdiagramm: Einbettung des CAN-Treibers zwischen BSW-Modulen und den physischen CAN-Controllern. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=11">CAN-Interface §1.1 „AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=36">CAN-Interface §7.6 „CAN Hardware Unit“</a></p> <h4>Initialisierung und Betriebsmodi der CAN-Controller</h4> <p> Der Lebenszyklus des Treibers beginnt in der Startphase des Gesamtsystems: Der ECU State Manager (EcuM) ruft synchron die Funktion <code>Can_Init</code> auf und übergibt dabei den Zeiger auf die treiberweite Konfigurationsstruktur <code>Can_ConfigType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00413" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00413">[SWS_Can_00413]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>). Hierbei initialisiert der Treiber statische Variablen, globale Register der CAN-Hardware-Einheit sowie controllerspezifische Parameter, verbleibt jedoch bezüglich der Netzwerkkommunikation in einem inaktiven Grundzustand (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=39">CAN-Interface §7.8 „Initialization“</a>). Das Gegenstück zur Initialisierung bildet <code>Can_DeInit</code>, welches die Baugruppe wieder in den Ausgangszustand zurückversetzt (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a>). </p> <p> Die Spezifikation abstrahiert die komplexen mikrocontrollerspezifischen Zustandsmaschinen der CAN-Hardware auf vier elementare Zustände des Aufzählungstyps <code>Can_ControllerStateType</code>: <code>CAN_CS_UNINIT</code>, <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code>, <code>CAN_CS_STARTED</code> und <code>CAN_CS_SLEEP</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>). Unmittelbar nach erfolgreicher Ausführung von <code>Can_Init</code> befinden sich alle Controller im Modus <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code>, in welchem weder das Senden noch das Empfangen von Nachrichten auf dem Bus möglich ist (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=39">CAN-Interface §7.8 „Initialization“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „CAN Controller Operation Modes“</a>). </p> <p> Zustandsübergänge werden asynchron durch die übergeordnete Schicht mittels <code>Can_SetControllerMode</code> angefordert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>). Der Treiber speichert die Zustände der Controller nicht eigenständig persistent als Softwarespeicher, sondern führt die Hardwareübergänge durch und meldet die vollzogene Transition über das Callback <code>CanIf_ControllerModeIndication</code> an das <code>CanIf</code> zurück (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>). Ergänzend kann der aktuelle Zustand jederzeit synchron über <code>Can_GetControllerMode</code> abgefragt werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91014">[SWS_Can_91014]</a>). </p> <div class="diagram" id="diag-can-controller-fsm"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" nach AUTOSAR. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a></p> <h4>Sende- und Empfangsarchitektur über Hardware-Objekte</h4> <p> Die Kopplung zwischen den logischen Kommunikationspuffern der oberen Schichten und den konkreten Hardware-Mailboxen des CAN-Controllers erfolgt über abstrakte Bezeichner, die sogenannten Hardware Object Handles (HOH) vom Typ <code>Can_HwHandleType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00429" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00429">[SWS_Can_00429]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=29">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Hardware object handles“</a>). Dabei wird unterschieden zwischen Sende-Handles (Hardware Transmit Handles, HTH) und Empfangs-Handles (Hardware Receive Handles, HRH) (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=29">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Hardware object handles“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=31">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Definition of HTH“</a>). Innerhalb einer Hardware-Einheit bilden sämtliche HOHs einen zusammenhängenden Nummerierungsbereich beginnend bei null (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=31">CAN-Interface §7.2 „Numbering area starting with zero“</a>). </p> <p> Zur Übertragung einer Nachricht übergibt <code>CanIf</code> dem Treiber über den synchronen Dienst <code>Can_Write</code> das Ziel-HTH sowie einen Zeiger auf die Datenstruktur <code>Can_PduType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=41">CAN-Interface §7.10 „Transmit data flow“</a>). Diese Struktur bündelt das Software-PDU-Handle (<code>swPduHandle</code>), die Nutzlänge (<code>length</code>), die Nutzdaten (<code>sdu</code>) sowie den CAN-Identifier (<code>id</code> vom Typ <code>Can_IdType</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00416" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00416">[SWS_Can_00416]</a>). Die zwei höchstwertigen Bits von <code>Can_IdType</code> kennzeichnen dabei das Frame-Format: Standard-CAN, Extended-CAN sowie deren jeweilige CAN-FD-Pendants (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00416" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00416">[SWS_Can_00416]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=33">CAN-Interface §7.4.1 „Dynamic Transmit L-PDUs“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=68">CAN-Interface §7.26 „CAN FD Support“</a>). </p> <p> Ist im Controller keine freie Sende-Mailbox verfügbar, weist der Treiber die Übertragungsanforderung ab und liefert den speziellen Statuswert <code>CAN_BUSY</code> (Wert 0x02) zurück (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=40">CAN-Interface §7.9 „Transmit request“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=43">CAN-Interface §7.11.2.1 „Storage of L-PDUs in the transmit L-PDU buffer“</a>). In diesem Fall obliegt es der Software-Pufferung im <code>CanIf</code>, die Nachricht zwischenzuspeichern und erneut zu übermitteln, sobald eine Mailbox frei wird (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=42">CAN-Interface §7.11.1 „General behavior“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=45">CAN-Interface §7.11.2.1 „Priority order“</a>). Sobald der Frame erfolgreich über das Netz versendet wurde, informiert der Treiber das <code>CanIf</code> via <code>CanIf_TxConfirmation</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=46">CAN-Interface §7.12 „Transmit confirmation“</a>). </p> <div class="diagram" id="diag-can-tx-sequence"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 690 499" font-family="Helvetica,sans-Serif" Pufferung und Bestätigung. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=41">CAN-Interface §7.10 „Transmit data flow“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=46">CAN-Interface §7.12 „Transmit confirmation“</a></p> <p> Im Empfangspfad werden eingehende Nachrichten hardwareseitig über HRHs erfasst. Die Architektur unterscheidet zwischen FullCAN-Objekten, die jeweils nur für eine einzelne feste CAN-ID konfiguriert sind, und BasicCAN-Objekten, die über Hardware-Filter ganze ID-Bereiche empfangen (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=37">CAN-Interface §7.7 „BasicCAN and FullCAN reception“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=38">CAN-Interface §7.7 „Hardware acceptance filter“</a>). Vor der Übergabe der empfangenen Daten an das <code>CanIf</code> via <code>CanIf_RxIndication</code> kann optional eine konfigurierte LPDU-Callout-Funktion ausgeführt werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00443" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00443">[SWS_Can_00443]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=47">CAN-Interface §7.13 „Receive data flow“</a>). Diese Callout-Funktion prüft die Frame-Daten auf Treiberebene; liefert sie <code>false</code>, wird die Weiterleitung abgebrochen, womit unzulässige oder irrelevante Frames frühzeitig gefiltert werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00443" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00443">[SWS_Can_00443]</a>). </p> <div class="diagram" id="diag-can-rx-activity"><svg 186.56,-36.29 176.15,-38.3 179.68,-44.35"></polygon> </g> </g> </svg></div> <p class="diagram-note">Aktivitätsdiagramm: Empfangsverarbeitung von CAN-Frames auf Treiberebene inklusive Callout-Entscheidung. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00443" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00443">[SWS_Can_00443]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=47">CAN-Interface §7.13 „Receive data flow“</a></p> <h4>Ereignisverarbeitung: Polling versus Interrupts</h4> <p> Zur Entkopplung von Busereignissen unterstützt der CAN-Treiber sowohl interruptgetriebene als auch zyklisch gepolte Betriebsarten. Für zeitkritische Abschnitte oder zur Realisierung von exklusiven Bereichen können die Controller-Interrupts synchron über <code>Can_DisableControllerInterrupts</code> gesperrt und über <code>Can_EnableControllerInterrupts</code> wieder freigegeben werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00231" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00231">[SWS_Can_00231]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00232" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00232">[SWS_Can_00232]</a>). </p> <p> Wird ein Kanal oder Ereignistyp im Polling-Modus betrieben, ruft der BSW-Scheduler (SchM) zyklisch die spezifischen Main-Functions des Moduls auf (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00225" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00225">[SWS_Can_00225]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00226" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00226">[SWS_Can_00226]</a>). Hierzu zählen <code>Can_MainFunction_Write</code> zur Abfrage getätigter Sendeübertragungen, <code>Can_MainFunction_Read</code> zur Bearbeitung empfangener Nachrichten, <code>Can_MainFunction_BusOff</code> zur Erkennung von Bus-Off-Zuständen, <code>Can_MainFunction_Wakeup</code> zur Erfassung von Weckereignissen sowie <code>Can_MainFunction_Mode</code> zur Überwachung von asynchronen Zustandsübergängen der Controller (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00225" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00225">[SWS_Can_00225]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00226" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00226">[SWS_Can_00226]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00227" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00227">[SWS_Can_00227]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00228" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00228">[SWS_Can_00228]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00368" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00368">[SWS_Can_00368]</a>). </p> <p> Im Weck- und Standby-Szenario dient die API <code>Can_CheckWakeup</code> der Überprüfung, ob ein spezifizierter Controller das Weckereignis des Steuergeräts ausgelöst hat (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00360" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00360">[SWS_Can_00360]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=55">CAN-Interface §7.18.4.1 „Wake-up detection“</a>). Dieses Verfahren ermöglicht es dem System, schlafende Controller gezielt zu identifizieren und den Kommunikationsstack bedarfsgerecht wieder in Betrieb zu nehmen (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=55">CAN-Interface §7.18.4.1 „Wake-up detection“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=56">CAN-Interface §7.18.4.1 „Wake-up validation“</a>). </p> <h4>Partitionierung und Mehrkernunterstützung</h4> <p> In modernen Steuergerätearchitekturen mit Multicore- und Sicherheitszonen-Aufteilung unterliegt der CAN-Treiber strengen Randbedingungen bezüglich der Speicher- und Partitionszuordnung. Gemäß <code>SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508</code> agiert das Modul in jeder ECUC-Partition als eigenständige Instanz, sodass API-Aufrufe stets nur die Ressourcen und Datenstrukturen derjenigen Partition betreffen, aus der heraus sie aufgerufen wurden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508]</a>). </p> <p> Die Konfigurationskonsistenz wird durch komplementäre Constraints abgesichert: Die durch <code>CanControllerEcucPartitionRef</code> referenzierten Partitionen müssen eine echte Teilmenge der globalen Treiber-Partitionsreferenzen (<code>CanEcucPartitionRef</code>) darstellen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509]</a>). Zudem müssen der CAN-Controller und der zugehörige Transceiver-Kanal eines physischen Kommunikationskanals zwingend dieselbe Partition referenzieren (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510]</a>). Konfigurationen mit Partitionszuordnungen, die von der jeweiligen Hardware- oder Software-Implementierung nicht unterstützt werden, weist das Modul strikt zurück (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00507" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00507">[SWS_Can_00507]</a>). </p> <h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4> <p> Der CAN-Treiber unterscheidet zwischen Fehlern im Software-Ablauf (Entwicklungs- und Laufzeitfehler) und Fehlern auf der physischen Bitebene des CAN-Busses (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>). Wird eine API mit ungültigen Zeigern aufgerufen, meldet der Treiber <code>CAN_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>). Fehlerhafte Handle-, Längen- oder Controller-Parameter führen zu <code>CAN_E_PARAM_HANDLE</code>, <code>CAN_E_PARAM_DATA_LENGTH</code> beziehungsweise <code>CAN_E_PARAM_CONTROLLER</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>). Der Aufruf von Diensten vor der Initialisierung wird über <code>CAN_E_UNINIT</code> signalisiert, unzulässige Moduswechsel lösen <code>CAN_E_TRANSITION</code> aus und fehlerhafte Baudrateneinstellungen werden mit <code>CAN_E_PARAM_BAUDRATE</code> quittiert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a>). Ein Verlust empfangener Nachrichten durch Pufferüberlauf in der Hardware wird als Laufzeitfehler <code>CAN_E_DATALOST</code> erfasst (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91020">[SWS_Can_91020]</a>). </p> <p> Zur Diagnose des Controller-Zustands auf dem Netzwerk stellt der Treiber Statusabfragen bereit. Über den Dienst <code>Can_GetControllerErrorState</code> lässt sich der aktuelle Fehlerstatus (<code>Can_ErrorStateType</code>) auslesen, welcher die Zustände <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_ACTIVE</code>, <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_PASSIVE</code> und <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF</code> umfasst (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a>). Während der Controller im aktiven Zustand vollwertig an der Kommunikation teilnimmt und aktive Error-Frames aussendet, sendet er im Zustand <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_PASSIVE</code> lediglich passive Fehlersignale; im Zustand <code>CAN_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF</code> ist er vollständig vom Bus isoliert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „CAN Controller Operation Modes“</a>). </p> <p> Über die APIs <code>Can_GetControllerRxErrorCounter</code> und <code>Can_GetControllerTxErrorCounter</code> können die internen Hardware-Fehlerzähler (REC und TEC) gezielt abgefragt werden (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>). Überschreitet der Sende-Fehlerzähler den Schwellwert zur Bus-Off-Kondition, meldet der Treiber dieses gravierende Ereignis über den Callback <code>CanIf_ControllerBusOff</code> an das <code>CanIf</code>, welches in der Folge das Zustandsmanagement (CanSM) und die PDU-Kanalmodi koordiniert (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „BusOff-Benachrichtigung“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=59">CAN-Interface §7.19.2.1 „CANIF_TX_OFFLINE bei BusOff“</a>). Zudem werden detaillierte Bit- und Protokollfehler wie Bit-Monitoring-, Acknowledge-, CRC- oder Stuffing-Fehler über den Typ <code>Can_ErrorType</code> klassifiziert und für Sicherheits- sowie Diagnosemechanismen bereitgestellt (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=69">CAN-Interface §7.27 „Security Events“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=70">CAN-Interface §7.27 „Security Events für Controller-Zustände“</a>). </p> <div class="diagram" id="diag-can-error-fsm"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewbox="0.00 0.00 1060.75 392.04" style="max-width:1414px"> <g id="graph0" class="graph" transform="scale(1 1) rotate(0) translate(14.4 377.64)"> <title>CanErrorStates</title> <!-- ACTIVE --> <g id="node1" class="node"> <title>ACTIVE</title> <ellipse fill="#ffffff" stroke="#01696f" stroke-width="1.2" cx="114.16" cy="-199.04" rx="114.16" ry="114.16"></ellipse> <text text-anchor="middle" x="114.16" y="-202.34" font-family="Helvetica,sans-Serif" font-size="11.00" fill="#01696f">CAN_ERRORSTATE_ACTIVE</text> <text text-anchor="middle" x="114.16" y="-189.14" font-family="Helvetica,sans-Serif" font-size="11.00" fill="#01696f">(REC &lt;= 127 &amp;&amp; Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00227" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00227">[SWS_Can_00227]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a></p> <h4>Weiterführende Detailbelege</h4> <p> Zur vertiefenden Betrachtung der Modulschnittstellen und Konfigurationsmechanismen dienen die folgenden Kernanforderungen und Dokumentstellen der AUTOSAR-Spezifikation: </p> <ul> <li> <strong>Modulinitialisierung und Konfiguration:</strong> Die strukturierte Bereitstellung der Konfigurationsdaten erfolgt über <code>Can_ConfigType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00413" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00413">[SWS_Can_00413]</a>), ausgeführt durch <code>Can_Init</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>) und rückgebaut via <code>Can_DeInit</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a>). Versionsinformationen liefert <code>Can_GetVersionInfo</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00224" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00224">[SWS_Can_00224]</a>). </li> <li> <strong>Controller-Zustandsverwaltung:</strong> Die Definitionen der Controller-Betriebszustände finden sich in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91010">[SWS_Can_91010]</a> und <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>; deren Steuerung erfolgt über <code>Can_SetControllerMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>) und <code>Can_GetControllerMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91014">[SWS_Can_91014]</a>) im Zusammenspiel mit <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=53">CAN-Interface §7.18.2 „CAN Controller Operation Modes“</a>. </li> <li> <strong>Datenübertragung und Hardware-Abstraktion:</strong> Sende- und Empfangsobjekte basieren auf <code>Can_HwHandleType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00429" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00429">[SWS_Can_00429]</a>) und den PDU-Definitionen in <code>Can_PduType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00415" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00415">[SWS_Can_00415]</a>) sowie <code>Can_IdType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00416" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00416">[SWS_Can_00416]</a>). Die Übermittlung steuert <code>Can_Write</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>) unter Berücksichtigung des Rückgabewerts <code>CAN_BUSY</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>) und Callbacks wie <code>CanIf_TxConfirmation</code> und <code>CanIf_RxIndication</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=20">CAN-Interface §5 „Hardware-Unabhängigkeit und Callbacks“</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=41">CAN-Interface §7.10 „Transmit data flow“</a>). </li> <li> <strong>Fehlerbehandlung und Busüberwachung:</strong> Die Klassifizierung von Entwicklungsfehlern wird in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91019" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91019">[SWS_Can_91019]</a> geregelt, Datenverlust in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91020">[SWS_Can_91020]</a>. Der Hardware-Fehlerstatus wird über <code>Can_ErrorStateType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>) und <code>Can_GetControllerErrorState</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a>) zusammen mit den Fehlerzählern (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>) und Protokollfehlertypen (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91021" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91021">[SWS_Can_91021]</a>) ermittelt. </li> <li> <strong>Multicore- und Partitions-Constraints:</strong> Die partitionsbezogene Instanziierung und Referenzintegrität ist normiert durch die Festlegungen in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510]</a> sowie <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00507" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00507">[SWS_Can_00507]</a>. </li> </ul> <p class="ai-note">Dieser Modul-Leitfaden wurde auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikationen für das Release R20-11 maschinell generiert.</p> </div>

Figure 1.1: AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model (see [7]) The CAN Interface module consists of all CAN hardware independent tasks, which belongs to the CAN communication device drivers of the corresponding ECU. Those functionality is implemented once in the CAN Interface module, so that underlying CAN device drivers only focus on access and control of the corresponding specific CAN hardware device. CanIf fulfils main control flow and data flow requirements of the PDU Router and upper layer communication modules of the AUTOSAR COM stack: transmit request processing , transmit confirmation / receive indication / error notification and start / stop of a CAN Controller and thus waking up / participating on a network . Its data processing and notification API is based on CAN L-SDUs , whereas APIs for control and mode handling provides a CAN Controller related view. In case of Transmit Requests CanIf completes the L-PDU transmission with cor- responding parameters and relays the CAN L-PDU via the appropriate CanDrv to

The CanDrv detects and processes events of the CAN Controllers and notifies those to the CanIf. The CanIf passes operation mode requests of the CanSm to the corresponding under- lying CAN Controllers. CanDrv provides a normalized L-PDU to ensure hardware independence of CanIf . The pointer to this normalized L-PDU points either to a temporary buffer (for e.g. data normalizing) or to the CAN hardware dependent CanDrv . For CanIf the kind of L-PDU buffer is invisible. The CanIf provides notification services used by the CanDrv in all notifications sce- narios, for example: transmit confirmation (subsection 8.4.2 CanIf_TxConfirmation, see [SWS_CANIF_00007]), receive indication (subsection 8.4.3 CanIf_RxIndication, see [SWS_CANIF_00006]) and notification of a controller mode change (subsection 8.4.8, see [SWS_CANIF_00699]). In case of using multiple CanDrv serving different interrupt vectors these callback ser- vices mentioned above must be re-entrant, refer to section 7.24 Multiple CAN Driver support. Reentrancy of callback functions is specified in section 8.4. The callback services called by the CanDrv are declared and implemented inside the CanIf. The callback services called by the CanIf are declared and placed inside the appropriate upper communication service layer, for example PduR, CanNm, CanTp. 7.2 Hardware object handles Hardware Object Handles ( HOH ) for transmission ( HTH ) as well as for reception ( HRH ) represent an abstract reference to a CAN mailbox structure , that contains CAN related parameters such as CanId , DLC and data . Based on the CAN hardware buffer abstraction each Hardware Object is referenced in CanIf independent of the CAN hardware buffer layout. The HOH is used as a parameter in the calls of CanDrv 's interface services and is provided by CanDrv 's configuration and used by CanDrv as identifier for communication buffers of the CAN mailbox. CanIf acts only as user of the Hardware Object Handle , but does not interpret it on the basis of hardware specific information. CanIf therefore remains independent of hardware. [SWS_CANIF_00023] ⌈ CanIf shall avoid direct access to hardware specific commu- nication buffers and shall access it exclusively via CanDrv interface services. ⌋ (SRS_- Can_01001) Rationale for [SWS_CANIF_00023]: CanIf remains independent of hardware, be- cause CanDrv interfaces are called with HOH parameters, which abstract from the concrete CAN hardware buffer properties. Each CAN Controller can provide multiple CAN Transmit Hardware Objects in the CAN mailbox. These can be logically linked to one entire pool of Hardware Objects (multiplexed Hardware Objects ) and thus addressed by one HTH . [SWS_CANIF_00662] ⌈ CanIf shall use two…

CanIf supports activation and deactivation of all L-PDUs belonging to one CAN Con- troller for transmission as well as for reception (see 7.19.2, see CanIf_SetPdu- Mode() , [SWS_CANIF_00008]). For L-PDU mode control refer to section 7.19. Each L-PDU is associated with an upper layer module in order to ensure correct dis- patching during reception, transmission confirmation, and data access. Each upper layer module can use the L-PDUs to serve different CAN Controllers simultane- ously. According to the PDU architecture defined for the entire AUTOSAR communication stack (see [7, Layered Software Architecture]), the usage of L-PDUs is split in two different ways: • For transmission request and transmission/reception polling API the upper layer module uses the L-SDU ID ( CanTxPduId / CanRxPduId ) defined by CanIf as parameter. • For all callback APIs, which are invoked by CanIf at upper layer modules, CanIf passes the target PduId defined by each upper layer module as parameter. The principle is that the caller must use the defined target L-PDU / L-SDU Id of the callee. If power on initialization is not performed and upper layer performs transmit requests to CanIf , no L-SDUs are transmitted to lower layer and DET shall be invoked. Thus, no un-initialized data can be transmitted on the network. Behavior of L-PDU / L-SDU transmitting function is specified in detail in subsection 8.…

Figure 7.3: Physical channel view definition example B 7.6 CAN Hardware Unit The CAN Hardware Unit combines one or multiple CAN Controller modules of the same type, which may be located on-chip or as external standalone devices. Each CAN Hardware Unit is served by the corresponding CanDrv . If different types of CAN Controllers are used, also different types of CanDrvs have to be applied with a unified API to CanIf . CanIf collects information about number and types of CAN Controllers and their Hardware Objects at configuration time. This allows transparent and hardware independent access to the CAN Controllers from upper layer modules using HOHs (refer to section 7.2 Hardware object handles and section 7.24 Multiple CAN Driver support). Figure 7.4 shows a CAN Hardware Unit consisting of two CAN Controllers of the same type connected to two physical channels:

▸ AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface, S. 37 inbound AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface (S. 37)

Figure 7.4: Typical CAN Hardware Unit 7.7 BasicCAN and FullCAN reception CanIf distinguishes between BasicCAN and FullCAN handling for activation of soft- ware acceptance filtering. A CAN mailbox ( Hardware Object ) for FullCAN operation only enables transmission or reception of single CanIds . Accordingly, BasicCAN operation of one Hardware Object enables to transmit or receive a range of CanIds . A Hardware Receive Object for configured BasicCAN reception is able to receive a range of CanIds , which pass its hardware acceptance filter. This range may exceed the list of predefined Rx L-PDUs to be received by this HRH . Therefore, CanIf subse- quently shall execute software filtering to pass only the predefined list of Rx L-PDUs to the corresponding upper layer modules. For more details please refer to section 7.20 Software receive filter.

This feature can be realized by different variants of implementations, no configuration options are available. 7.8 Initialization The EcuM calls the CanIf's function CanIf_Init() for initialization of the entire CanIf (see [SWS_CANIF_00001]). All global variables and data structures are initialized including flags and buffers during the initialization process. The EcuM executes initial- ization of CanDrvs and CanTrcvs separately by call of their corresponding initialization services (refer to [1] and [2, Specification of CAN Transceiver Driver]). The CanIf expects that the CAN Controller remains in STOPPED mode like af- ter power-on reset after the initialization process has been completed. In this mode the CanIf and CanDrv are neither able to transmit nor receive CAN L-PDUs (see [SWS_CANIF_00001]). If re-initialization of the entire CAN modules during runtime is required, the EcuM shall invoke the CanSm (see [3]) to initiate the required state transitions of the CAN Con- troller by call of CAN Interface module's API service CanIf_SetControllerMode () . The CanIf maps the calls from CanSm to calls of the respective CanDrvs (see subsection 8.6.3). 7.9 Transmit request CanIf 's transmit request function CanIf_Transmit() ([SWS_CANIF_00005]) is a common interface for upper layers to transmit L-PDUs on the CAN network. The access to the L-SDU specific data is organized by the following parameters: • Transmit L-PDU => L-SDU ID • Reference to a data structure, which contains L-SDU related data: Pointer to the L-SDU , pointer to the MetaData and L-SDU length. The reference to the L-SDU data structure is used as a parameter in several CanIf 's API services, e.g. CanIf_Transmit() or the callback service <User_RxIndica- tion>() . In case the L-PDU is configured for triggered transmission, the L-SDU pointer is a null pointer.

7.11 Transmit buffering 7.11.1 General behavior At the scope of CanIf the transmit process starts with the call of CanIf_Transmit() and it ends with invocation of upper layer module's callback service <User_TxCon- firmation>() . During the transmit process CanIf , CanDrv and the CAN Mailbox altogether shall store the L-PDU to be transmitted only once at a single location. De- pending on the transmit method, these are: • The CAN hardware transmit object or • The Transmit L-PDU Buffer inside CanIf , if transmit buffering is enabled. For triggered transmission, CanIf only has to store the transmit request for the given L-PDU but not its data. The data is fetched just in time by means of the trigger transmit function when the HTH is free (again). A single Tx L-PDU , requested for transmission, shall never be stored twice. This behavior corresponds to the usual way of periodic communication on the CAN network. If transmit buffering is enabled, CanIf will store a Tx L-PDU in a CanIf Trans- mit L-PDU Buffer ( CanIfBufferCfg ), if it is rejected by CanDrv at Transmit Request . Basically, the overall buffer in CanIf for buffering Tx L-PDUs consits of one or multi- ple CanIfBufferCfg (see CanIfBufferCfg ). Whereas each CanIfBufferCfg is assigned to one or multiple dedicated CanIfBufferHthRef (see CanIfBuffer- HthRef ) and can be configured to buffer one or multiple Tx L-PDUs . But as al…

In case of a new reception of an L-PDU CanDrv calls CanIf_RxIndication() (refer to [SWS_CANIF_00006]) of CanIf . The access to the L-PDU specific data is orga- nized by these parameters: • Hardware Receive Handle ( HRH ) • Received CAN Identifier (CanId) • Received Data Length • Reference to Received L-PDU The Received L-PDU is hardware dependent (nibble and byte ordering, access type) and allocated to the lowest layer in the communication system - to CanDrv . HRH serves as a link between CanDrv and the upper layer module using the L-PDU . The HRH identifies one CAN hardware receive object, where a new CAN L-PDU was received. After the indication of a received L-PDU by CanDrv ( CanIf_RxIndication() is called) the CanIf shall proceed as described in 7.14 Receive indication. CanIf is not able to recognize, whether CanDrv uses temporary buffering or a direct hardware access. It expects normalized L-PDU data in calls of the CanIf_RxIndication() . The CAN hardware receive object is locked until the end of the copy process to the tem- porary or upper layer module buffer. The hardware object will be immediately released after CanIf_RxIndication() of CanIf returns to avoid loss of data. CanDrv , CanIf and the upper layer module, which belongs to the received L-PDU , access the same temporary intermediate buffer, which can be located either in the CAN hardware receive object of the CAN…

The upper layer modules initiate the receive request only via CanIf services without direct access to CanDrv . The initiated receive request is suc- cessfully completed, if CanIf wrote the received L-SDU into the upper layer module I-PDU buffer. The function CanIf_ReadRxPduData() makes reading out data without dependence of reception event (RxIndication) possible. When it is enabled at configuration time (see CanIfPublicReadRxPduDataApi ), not necessarily a receive indication service for the same L-SDU has to be configured (see CanIfRxPduUserRxIndicationUL ). 7.18.4.1 Wake-up detection If wake-up support is enabled (see [SWS_CANIF_00180]) CanIf is notified by the Integration Code about a detected CAN wake-up by the service CanIf_CheckWakeup () (see CAN Wakeup Sequences of [13]). In case of a CAN bus " wake-up " event the function CanIf_CheckWakeup(Wakeup- Source) may be called during execution of EcuM_CheckWakeup(WakeupSource) (see wake-up sequence diagrams of EcuM ). CanIf in turn checks by configured input reference to EcuMWakeupSource in CanDrvs , which CanDrvs have to be checked. CanIf gets this information via reference CanIfCtrlCanCtrlRef . The Communication Service, which is called, belongs to the service defined during configuration (see CanIfDispatchCfg ). In this way EcuM as well as CanSm are able to change CAN Controller States and to control the system behavior concerning the BusOff recovery or wake-up procedure . • A smaller range is more relevant than a larger range. ⌋ () 7.20.2 Software filter algorithms The choice of suitable software search algorithms it is up to the implementation of CanIf . According to the wide range of possible receive BasicCAN operations provided by the CAN Controller it is recommended to offer several search algorithms like linear search, table search and/or hash search variants to provide the most optimal solution for most use cases. 7.21 Data Length Check The received Data Length value is compared with the configured Data Length value of the received L-PDU. The configured Data Length value shall be derived from the size of used bytes inside this L-PDU. The configured Data Length value may not be necessarily that Data Length value defined in the CAN communication matrix and used by the sender of this CAN L-PDU. [SWS_CANIF_00026] ⌈ CanIf shall accept all received L-PDUs (see [SWS_CANIF_00390]) with a Data Length value equal or greater then the configured Data Length value (see CanIfRxPduDataLength ). ⌋ (SRS_Can_01005) [SWS_CANIF_00902] ⌈ The Data Length Check shall be processed if it is enabled globally (see CanIfPrivateDataLengthCheck ) and not disabled individually per PDU (see CanIfRxPduDataLengthCheck ). ⌋ () Hint: If the Data Length Check is disabled globally, it can't be enabled individually per PDU. [SWS_CANIF_00168] ⌈ If the Data Length Check rejects…

The support for multiple CanDrvs can be enabled and disabled by the configuration parameter CanIfPublicMultipleDrvSupport . 7.24.1 Transmit requests by using multiple CAN Drivers Each Transmit L-PDU enables CanIf to derive the corresponding CAN Con- troller and implicitly CanDrv serving the affected Hardware Unit . Resolving of these dependencies is possible because of the construction of the CAN Controller Handle : it combines CanDrv Handle and the corresponding CAN Controller in the Hardware Unit . At configuration time a CAN Controller Handle will be mapped to each CAN Con- troller . The sequence diagram Figure 7.10 below demonstrates two transmit re- quests directed to different CanDrvs . CanIf needs only to select the corresponding CanDrv in order to call the correct API service. Note: Figure 7.10 and the following table serve only as an example. Finally, it is up to the implementation to access the correct APIs of underlying CanDrvs .

Besides, the higher baud rate for the payload CAN FD also supports an extended payload which allows the transmission of up to 64 bytes. If these features are available depends on the general CAN FD support by the CAN Controller and if the CAN Controller is in CAN FD mode (valid CanControllerFdBaudrateConfig ). ⌋ () [SWS_CANIF_00913] ⌈ If security event reporting has been enabled for the CanIf module ( CanIfEnableSecurityEventReporting = true) the respective security events shall bereported to the IdsM via the interfaces defined in AUTOSAR_SWS_- BSWGeneral . ⌋ (RS_Ids_00810) [SWS_CANIF_00915] ⌈ If CanIf_ErrorNotification() is called by CanDrv , the function shall evaluate whether a Tx related error was detected. If this is the case the CanIf shall report the security event CANIF_SEV_TX_ERROR_DETECTED. The context data is structured as follows: Context Data (2 Byte) • ControllerID (1 Byte) • CanError (1 Byte)  CAN_ERROR_BIT_MONITORING1 (0x1)  CAN_ERROR_BIT_MONITORING0 (0x2)  CAN_ERROR_BIT (0x3)  CAN_ERROR_CHECK_ACK_FAILED (0x4)  CAN_ERROR_ACK_DELIMITER (0x5)  CAN_ERROR_ARBITRATION_LOST (0x6)  CAN_ERROR_OVERLOAD (0x7) ⌋ (RS_Ids_00810) [SWS_CANIF_00916] ⌈ If CanIf_ErrorNotification() is called by CanDrv , the function shall evaluate whether a Rx related error was detected. If this is the case the CanIf shall report the security event CANIF_SEV_RX_ERROR_DETECTED .

The context data is structured as follows: Context Data (2 Byte) • ControllerID (1 Byte) • CanError (1 Byte)  CAN_ERROR_CHECK_FORM_FAILED (0x8)  CAN_ERROR_CHECK_STUFFING_FAILED (0x9)  CAN_ERROR_CHECK_CRC_FAILED (0xA)  CAN_ERROR_BUS_LOCK (0xB) ⌋ (RS_Ids_00810) [SWS_CANIF_00917] ⌈ If CanIf_ControllerErrorStatePassive() is called by CanDrv , the CanIf shall report the security event CANIF_SEV_ERRORSTATE_PAS- SIVE in following cases: • TxErrorCounter > 127 and TxErrorCounter <= 255 • RxErrorCounter > 127 and TxErrorCounter <= 255 The context data is structured as follows: Context Data (2 Byte) • ControllerID (1 Byte) • ErrorCounterThreshold (1 Byte)  TxErrorCounter > 127 AND RxErrorCounter > 127(0x0)  TxErrorCounter > 127 AND RxErrorCounter < 127 (0x1)  RxErrorCounter > 127 AND TxErrorCounter < 127 (0x2) ⌋ (RS_Ids_00810) [SWS_CANIF_00918] ⌈ If CanIf_ControllerBusOff is called by CanDrv , the CanIf shall report the security event CANIF_SEV_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF . The context data is structured as follows: Context Data (1 Byte) • Controller ID (1 Byte) ⌋ (RS_Ids_00810) 7.28 Error classification [SWS_CANIF_00223] ⌈ For all defined production errors it is only required to report the event, when an error or diagnostic relevant event (e.g. state changes, no L-PDU events) occurs.
